# Summary

Update CAPRMEDIO Markdown Atoms

## Scope

Same-identity updates of exact selected Markdown Atom Carriers by the ATOM_UPDATE Tool.

## Claim

the ATOM_UPDATE Tool **must** provide same-identity updates of the frontmatter, content, **or** both for exact selected Markdown Atoms:

- preserve the Carrier path, filename, Atom identity, Type **and** Summary. do **not** assign an ID **to** an unassigned Draft merely **to** update its Carrier. every Summary or Type value change requires replacement with a new Atom ID and predecessor archival, **not** a same-ID update.
- resolve the admitted change class against the exact current Revision **and** proposal under CA-R-1432, reusing the current identity assessment under CA-O-067 where applicable. Every actual changed same-ID Atom update, including carrier-only, equivalent refinement and Status-only edits, advances Version by **`=1`** and preserves the exact prior Revision as required by the governing history rules. Change-class assessment does not waive the increment. replacement-required **or** uncertain classification must stop this update rather than silently changing identity **or** assuming permission.
- refresh Updated At **to** the actual accepted edit instant under CA-R-1788 for **every** accepted edit, including formatting-only **and** lossless-serialization edits. an actual no-op creates no fictitious edit, Version, timestamp refresh **or** archive effect; retain its truthful result for the governing Run contract.
- reject duplicate, missing, ambiguous, invalid, **or** stale explicit targets; preflight each one-Atom Action before its effect. Modify does not silently Find or substitute targets.
- modify **`=1`** explicit Atom target per Action with its expected Revision or digest. Preserve that Action's verified mutable before-frontier and storage-effect safeguards on effect or postcondition failure. A several-Atom Workflow stops at its first failed Action, retains completed Actions and leaves remaining targets untouched; do not promise cross-Atom rollback or all-or-nothing success.
- permit reuse of generic metadata **or** Relation-patch mechanics while retaining responsibility for Atom authority validation, admitted change class, Revision, one-Atom storage-effect safeguards, **and** effect semantics.
- default **to** mutation-free dry run. accept `--apply` **only** through authorized Project-local MCP delegation with a sealed Initiative action envelope.

The Tool **must** also accept the additional closed Subject-only preview root
`{atoms, subject_profile?}`. Every Atom item is exactly
`{selector, expected, subject_patches}`, where
`expected = {atom_id, version, sha256}`. Unknown root or item keys **must**
fail. Each replacement `subject_patches` entry has `field = governs|depends_on`,
exact `old` and explicit `new` values. For `depends_on`, the current value
`old` must identify exactly one existing list entry; a caller-supplied index
is not admitted. An Atom item using `subject_patches` must not also request
complete-frontmatter or body replacement. The selected files must be unique
within the payload.

Logical Property edits additionally support explicit add, replace and remove; list edits support entry add/remove, replacement by unique current value or complete-set replacement under CA-R-1934-TOOL_WORKFLOWS-CORE-REQUIREMENT--edit-atom-properties-by-current-values. Section edits follow CA-R-1933-TOOL_WORKFLOWS-CORE-REQUIREMENT--edit-one-explicit-atom-section. Every Summary value change requires a new Atom ID and predecessor archival through the replacement Workflow, even when the Claim remains unchanged.

Subject-only preview **must** select a complete original Atom Carrier with a stable Atom ID, excluding Draft and archived carriers by both carried Status and placement. Both the pinned source and proposed result **must** pass existing complete-carrier validation, including the applicable Content Role/Type Status model and correct Carrier placement. Preserve the carried Status byte-for-byte; do not activate the source or perform a lifecycle transition. Missing, ambiguous, unsupported, or stale validation authority **must** fail closed.

Omitted `subject_profile` selects `legacy`; `approved` is explicit; unknown or malformed supplied profiles **must** fail. Subject patches apply only to direct structured `subjects.governs` and `subjects.depends_on` fields, and the selected profile validates both the source and resulting scalar Subjects. Legacy uses `/` bearer qualification and `:` allowed values with literal dots and rejects every `atom(...)` selector. Approved uses `/` broader-to-narrower, `.` bearer-to-dependent, and `:` Property-to-allowed-value, and accepts only the exact initial lowercase selector forms registered by CA-R-1321. `Atom` and `atom` remain distinct; both profiles reject `@`, escapes, every other selector construction, conjunctions, wildcards, evaluation, aliases, and profile inference in Subject syntax. This is syntax validation only and does not enumerate selector instances, admit a target, or add an apply path.

Subject patches **must** reject a malformed or nested legacy Subjects shape, an
absent or ambiguous current value, a stale pin, an escaped or symlink target, or a
duplicate resulting dependency. The Tool **must** retain complete-carrier
validation and preserve every unrelated byte and line ending. A successful
Subject value change is a semantic revision with Version `N + 1`; a no-op
creates no revision. The preview result **must** return the selected
`subject_profile` and `subject_profile_evidence` containing exactly
`grammar_pins` and `native_admission: "not_performed"`; every grammar pin
contains `atom_id`, `version`, `path`, and `sha256`, and preview seals those
fields in its digest. Legacy cites the five exact historical definitions and
approved cites the five current definitions. Local use remains preview-only; an
illustrative preview timestamp is not an execution receipt. This mode does not
repair, migrate, infer ontology, adopt a Subject grammar, or add a standalone apply path.

The local wrapper **may** provide opt-in `run --stage-preview` for this same closed Subject-only payload, without changing the default dry run. Reject this option with generic update input or `--apply` before creating staged artifacts. Export only the existing illustrative proposed Carriers into a fresh Tool-generated `.caprmedio_tmp/subject-preview/<opaque-id>/` batch under CA-D-425's safe layout. Do not write authoritative originals, history, Journal, or promotion effects. Candidate Version/time remain illustrative; no-op metadata remain unchanged.

Staging **must** independently read back exact candidate bytes and SHA-256, run real complete-carrier validation against each original logical source path and applicable Status, then recheck source/identity/grammar pins using the same illustrative time. Return CA-D-425's separate closed manifest only after the whole batch passes; source drift must refuse success rather than refresh a preview. On failure report retained partial artifacts without a success seal or unsafe cleanup. Staged files are point-in-time review evidence, never effect approval.

CA-M-371 defines the same-profile preview method. The historical
`@<version>` archive filename convention remains a Delivery concern and is not
a Subject operator. CA-O-030 defines the operational Action. CA-E-304 supplies
its automated conformance cases **without** duplicating them **in** this
capability Requirement.

## Details

The logical Workflow owns Subject eligibility, selected profile, proposal, Version, preview and effect admission; its connector receives explicit logical targets, deltas and bound source/schema/permission evidence through the coherent interface. The closed legacy CLI payload and Markdown staging layout below are private existing implementation bindings, not a new universal connector schema. This authority split moves no code and does not establish that the existing implementation admits the new connector contract.

### Instructed Subjects-only batch

The Operator's explicit instruction authorizes the exact ordered Subjects-only map through the existing request Initiative and Operator authorization. Retain the instruction/request and packet bindings in execution context; do not require a separate form, content-review round, review/pause response or batch-confirmation receipt, and never fabricate one. The map binds each selected Atom's canonical target, exact current Version/SHA-256, Subject profile and explicit ordered patches. It does not authorize unlisted targets, held sources or ordinary content changes.

For the instructed draft-backed flow, commit current state, create the full edit drafts, commit the drafts, archive each exact current predecessor and promote its draft through the existing updater, then rebuild the entity graph through its existing operation only after the batch completes. The caller composes these existing operations and records their actual results; no new Tool family, executor or recovery gate is introduced. A separately instructed map-only batch remains available without draft staging.

Before each independent effect, retain the normal local target/draft/patch/layout, current-source, conditional-write, archive, Version/time and readback checks. Do not add a separate full-candidate validation pass, semantic content review or initial intent-metadata gate. Fresh native intent may be derived internally at the operation; no initial `subject_intent_sha256` is required in the public batch effect frontier. Only declared Subjects plus exactly N+1 and actual Updated At may change; preserve canonical ID, Summary, Type, original Status, placement and every unrelated byte. Restore the original Status from the temporary draft marker; an Active source therefore promotes to Active without changing generic non-Active semantics.

Advance in packet order only after verified applied or truthful no-op results. Stop at the first failed, refused, stale, canceled or uncertain member, retain completed effects and leave remaining and held sources untouched. Keep existing native failed-write restoration/error handling, but introduce no automatic batch rollback, replay, retry or resume. Report actual effects and any logging failure separately; a log is observation, not permission or proof of completion.

### Existing-Atom edit-draft staging and promotion

CA-D-446's explicitly source-pinned edit draft is the full proposed next Revision in the owning role's `draft/` folder. Replace the source filename's canonical ID once with `<canonical-ID>@draft`; carry that temporary proposal ID and `status: Draft`, leaving the canonical source untouched. Preserve complete source metadata/body outside declared Subjects and the temporary ID/Status and proposed Version/time markers. A changed proposal shows N+1 and illustrative time; a true no-op keeps source Version/time. This is not another canonical original, new Atom identity or globally admitted suffixed ID.

The existing `atom_update` Tool accepts `{operation: "stage_subject_batch", subject_batch: {path, digest}, limit?}` under CA-D-531. `limit` is a strict integer 1..10, default 10. Each call creates at most that many drafts with normal safe create-only/no-follow file checks and readback, changes no canonical/history files, and returns compact actual progress: `operation`, `state: "staging"|"staged"|"stopped"`, `count`, `completed`, `remaining`, `stage_run_id`, and `reviewed_packet: {path, digest}|null`, plus actual failure evidence. Only completed staging returns the final schema1 packet pinning every draft. Preserve truthful partial artifacts; never report partial work as completed.

For this batch, local carrier parsing, exact descriptors, explicit old-value patches, selected grammar, safe layout, deterministic byte materialization and conditional-write/readback are the normal checks; do not repeatedly revalidate unchanged body content or build a global reference inventory for every member. The existing final graph operation remains separate.

No separate full-candidate validation, content-review or confirmation round follows staging or the draft commit. Existing request authorization carries the instructed promotion. At each target's operation reopen the exact pinned current/draft bytes, normalize the temporary ID and Status to the canonical ID and original Status, and apply the normal native Subjects-only patch/layout, archive, metadata and conditional-write/readback checks. A full proposal does not authorize any additional metadata/body delta. Use actual effect time and the existing exact predecessor archive; fail on source/draft drift without silently rebinding. Same-MCP-connection staging is unnecessary. Existing first-failure and native failed-write handling remain; no automatic batch rollback or replay is introduced. After verified canonical output and any required predecessor readback, conditionally remove only that member's exact packet-pinned draft bytes. If draft cleanup fails or its bytes have drifted, stop and report the actual cleanup failure, preserving the published canonical Revision and archive; do not roll them back or remove another file.

### Ordinary one-target Subject update

The existing Project-local MCP `update_atom` route **must** also accept the closed Subject-only parameter variant defined by CA-D-531: `{target, subject_patches, subject_intent_sha256, subject_profile?, semantic_assessment_report?}`. It selects exactly one complete current original Carrier and reuses the preview's eligibility, exact scalar-patch, same-profile, complete-carrier and byte-preservation checks. Reject mixed generic replacement fields, unknown fields, projection or delivered copies, owner/path mismatch, competing non-archived originals, and an unsafe or unverifiable claimed competing owner. Bulk preview does not authorize bulk lifecycle execution.

The mutation-free preparation **must** return CA-D-425's deterministic `subject_intent` and `subject_intent_sha256`. For a value change, derive the complete intended proposal by changing only Subjects while retaining the old Version and Updated At for CA-O-067's assessment. Reuse the current completed Analysis Report and exact CA-O-145 assessment under CA-R-1892 and CA-D-585; syntax validation and a caller-supplied class are not identity or lineage evidence. An unresolved, replacement-required, stale, or mismatched assessment prevents this effect.

Application **must** consume CA-D-527's exact authorized execute envelope through the existing selected route, actual selected execution session and actual CA-O-030 Action start retained in the selected Run, with the exact completed CA-O-145 assessment. A caller Boolean, adapter envelope, local preview, candidate acceptance, or direct internal call grants no apply authority. Recheck all source, grammar, report, validation, definition, permission and destination evidence before effects.

A changed current Carrier **must** retain ID, Summary, Status, path, filename, every unrelated byte and line ending; set Version exactly to `N+1`; and materialize Updated At once from actual Project time at the effect. Preserve the exact predecessor bytes at Version `N` in the existing Delivery-governed history location, classified as archived history by placement, without a second Version increment or invented status/time edit. Verify actual after bytes and hash and bind them to the intended hash in the shared result. No-op creates no Carrier/history/change event; retain the actual Run observation without inventing a change. A caught publication/postcondition error requires an attempt to restore the verified mutable before-frontier and remove attempt-owned history only; failed or unverified restoration is not success and never permits automatic effect replay. Journal append/read has no prior-history, chain, validation, receipt, deduplication, retry or recovery prerequisite and does not gate or prove source-effect completion; report any actual recording I/O failure truthfully without replaying the effect. Abrupt crash or interruption is not crash-atomic: retain interrupted disposition and inspect actual affected current/history files and Run evidence before any separately admitted continuation. The local `ATOM_UPDATE --apply` guard and generic request behavior remain unchanged.

### Selected Subject publication access model

For ordinary one-target Subject publication outside the reviewed batch branch, stage and review the exact source-bound change before a short exclusive window over the affected current Carrier, predecessor-history destination and governing authority sources. Reuse the existing sealed source/delta/intent, assessment, permission and Run bindings; review is not effect permission. Staged candidate metadata remain illustrative. Actual Version and Updated At are materialized under the existing effect-time rule, not fixed by candidate review.

The existing `authorization_ref` **must** resolve a fresh purpose-specific trusted-host record of the Operator's explicit review of the exact source-bound intended change and confirmation to pause manual editing, maintenance/script writes, Git and synchronization for its affected current/history/authority frontier. A form response from the connected Codex Session is sufficient Operator confirmation when the form shows that exact request, selected Session/Run, intended change and affected files and explicitly confirms both review and the pause; no separate identity proof is required. Tool arguments, client names, model assertions, caller-written JSON or hashes and arbitrary callbacks never count as that response. Bind the record to the exact existing request, source/delta/intent, selected Session/Run and affected files; recheck it before effects. Issue the nonserializable one-use confirmation privately and consume it through the existing selected dispatch in the same process; the public API, route and request fields remain unchanged. Decline, cancel, malformed response, timeout, disconnect, unavailable issuer/resolver, missing or mismatched confirmation and any bound-evidence drift refuse before effects. This accepted trust model authorizes building the connection, not publication or runtime activation.

For this one changed Subject-only execute request, the existing connected Project-local MCP host may perform the admitted selected dispatch in the same process that owns the actual Codex request/session and issues the one-use confirmation, instead of enqueueing DBOS work. It must reuse the same closed request, exact current admission, saved request and selected Run/lifecycle implementation, validation, assessment, permission, restoration and truthful actual Run observations in the plain Project Journal. This exception changes dispatch placement only. Generic updates and every other selected operation retain the existing queue path. An unavailable or unconfirmed Subject exception refuses before effects; it is not permission to serialize confirmation, invent an endpoint or silently dispatch elsewhere.

During that window, no manual editing, maintenance/script write, Git operation or synchronization may change the affected sources, history or authority. Recheck the exact admitted frontier before effects; unavailable window, stale evidence or failed admission stops before effects. Preserve the window through current/history effects, independent readback and any existing Action-local restoration. No project-wide Engine write lock or replacement is required; distinct existing resource-specific locks remain unchanged. Retain all existing identity, complete-carrier, byte-preservation, ownership, restoration and truthful failure requirements.

This access model does not exclude other Engine writers and cannot protect against writers ignoring the exclusive window and does not itself establish crash-atomic multi-Carrier publication or a stronger guarantee. It does not waive an existing safety requirement, add effect permission or introduce retry/recovery policy. Live changed-Subject publication remains blocked until the selected model's actual binding and combined checks are independently accepted; choosing this model or revising sources does not remove the existing guard.

The by-current-value, Property and section contracts state required behavior; previous scalar-index fixtures are historical evidence and do not establish acceptance of this behavior. This source revision is neither implementation nor an execution receipt. Resume and retry policy for independent multi-Atom Actions remains deferred.

### Direct Subject preparation

ATOM_UPDATE also admits CA-D-425's direct MCP preview_subjects and stage_subjects operations. They are preparation Tool calls, not actual Atom-update Action Runs: preview writes nothing; explicit stage writes only fresh derived candidates and their manifest in the fixed Project scratch layout. They create no Session, Action Run, canonical Journal, authoritative Carrier or history effect. Actual enclosing-Step Tool-call recording and the existing Workflow semantic policy owner remain unchanged.

Direct input uses explicit logical Atom ID, Version, SHA-256 and selected profile. Support only implemented scalar/by-current-value replacement and complete dependency-set replacement; reject add/remove, generic edits, indexes and physical selectors. Preserve full selected-source/result validation, eligibility, identity/grammar/currentness and byte-preservation safeguards. Preparation supplies review evidence for later assessment without requiring or claiming completed O067/O145 assessment. Native staging must compare its own preview with the requested reviewed seal before any scratch creation, retaining same-time final revalidation. No supplied hash, candidate or manifest grants source-effect permission. Actual publication's source-effect admission guards remain unchanged; Journal recording is plain observation, not an admission or completion gate.

# Summary

## Scope

Workflow admission owns identity, Version/time, lifecycle and complete schema decisions. Connector calls use CA-D-625 only to verify the supplied request, source preconditions and permission and to perform the explicit mechanical operation. A connector does not choose those decisions.

One sealed Atom Modify action, including identity-preserving change classes, exact current state and prior semantic history; ordered actions remain independent.

## Claim

ATOM_UPDATE follows CA-R-866 and CA-O-030 for one Atom action, preserving identity, Summary, placement and exact prior semantic history with Version +1 for every actual changed same-ID update and actual edit-time results; no-op preserves Version and time. A later failed action cannot undo an earlier completed Atom action.

## Details

### Test cases

1. Prepare valid one-Atom semantic, frontmatter/content and unassigned Draft updates with exact identity, Version, timestamp, digest, proposal and admitted change class. For an ordered list of independent actions, include different classes and record each dry-run preview separately.
2. Reject repeated, missing, ambiguous, invalid, unauthorized, stale or uncertain-class input before the affected action writes. Change the second source after preview: an earlier completed action remains, the second fails and later actions are not started. Apply valid independent actions only with their own sealed permission and source-state evidence.
3. request a Summary change while retaining the Atom ID, including a changed heading **and** a filename Summary Slug change. reject it as a same-ID update even **if** the Claim is unchanged; report the need for replacement **without** silently allocating **or** applying a successor.
4. Apply formatting-only, lossless Subject serialization, equivalent refinement, Status-only and semantic changes with fixed Summary/Type. Every actual changed same-ID update requires exactly Version N+1 and actual refreshed Updated At, preserving exact prior state at N. A no-op keeps Version/time and creates no history effect. A Summary or Type change requires replacement instead. Keep content/class assessment truthful; a changed Claim, applicability, Subject target or Relation meaning is not equivalent merely because serialization is lossless.
5. Inject failure after an effect or publication and before verification within one Atom action. Compare that action's complete admitted restoration boundary, including its current Carrier and new history destination. Preserve earlier completed Atom actions; failed or unverified restoration is not a passing rollback.
6. request an evidenced unchanged result. distinguish actual no-op from an accepted carrier edit: require no invented Version, Updated At **or** archive mutation. retain the actual no-op/result evidence for the governing Run; file equality alone does **not** establish its actual execution.

### Logical modification cases

Required future cases cover CA-R-1933/CA-M-373 section add, replace, remove, title and position; CA-R-1934/CA-M-374 Property add, replace and remove; list entry add/remove, replacement of one entry by its exact current value, and replacement of the complete set. Require unique value resolution, reject caller list indexes, missing/ambiguous values and malformed final state, and preserve unrelated content. Every Summary change, including wording-only edits, rejects same-ID Modify and requires separately authorized fresh-ID replacement. Find and Read do not run implicitly. These cases are specifications, not observed passes.

### Subject-only update cases

Use an independently authored before/after byte ledger, not the graph builder, with complete valid Atom carriers. The required Subject-only replacement request is `atoms: [{selector, expected: {atom_id, version, sha256}, subject_patches: [{field: governs|depends_on, old: exact current value, new: explicit value}]}]`. Resolve a dependency by its unique exact current value; caller indexes are rejected. Subject-only add/remove/full-set changes use CA-D-623's explicit list operation shapes, preserving this mode's separation from generic content edits. Reject duplicate-file selectors and any request that mixes this mode with full `frontmatter` or `content` replacement; `both` is a lookup selector, not an update field.

Apply valid exact list-item changes in each direction by their unique current values; reorder the source list before a fresh request to prove selection does not depend on caller positions. The update must replace the selected Subject value only; a same value in body text does not satisfy `old`. Prefix matching is not a replacement operation: the lookup Evaluation covers exact and delimiter-boundary `/` and `:` cases, while this operation requires the exact old value and explicit new value. Do not reinterpret the pending relation grammar.

Reject before writing when the Atom ID, Version, SHA-256, field or old value is stale, wrong, missing or ambiguous; when Subjects are malformed, nested, missing, duplicated ambiguously, or the final dependency list would contain duplicate values; or when the requested path is absolute, escapes the approved root, is a symlink, a projection, or is missing. Do not repair any rejected carrier. Validate the complete resulting carrier, including frontmatter schema, identity, Subjects and uniquely resolved list values, before publication.

For an accepted non-no-op Subject change, require Version `+1` and an actual edit-time Updated At. Preserve all unrelated frontmatter and body bytes, unknown keys, formatting, and CRLF/LF line endings; only the explicit Subject list item and required Version/Updated At may differ. The default local preview is deterministic and writes nothing; opt-in staging writes only derived candidates under CA-D-425. Do not claim a new MCP binding. A no-op requires the complete intended Carrier to remain byte-for-byte unchanged. An equal replacement value or semantically equal list alone is not sufficient: changed serialization, ordering or any other Carrier bytes are an actual change and require Version +1 with actual time and exact prior history. Recheck the expected pins at apply time, and prove the unchanged standalone `ATOM_UPDATE --apply` guard still rejects unsupported direct apply. Inject a failed validation or publication and prove the fixture returns byte-for-byte to its before ledger.

Use valid stable-ID non-archived originals under their admitted Status models, including correctly placed Plan Done and Backlog carriers. Prove both source and result pass the real complete-carrier validator without mocking it; retain the Active case. Verify exact Status, Summary, identity, placement, unrelated frontmatter, body bytes, and line endings remain unchanged in the proposed Carrier except for the declared Subject and required Version/Updated At spans. Reject Draft or archived Status/placement, invalid role-specific Status, status-folder mismatch, unavailable or ambiguous validation authority, and any otherwise invalid complete source or result without repair or writes. ### Subject-profile preview cases

The closed Subject-only root envelope is exactly `{atoms, subject_profile?}`; each atom item remains exactly `{selector, expected, subject_patches}`. The exact path selector is a source locator, not Subject syntax. Exercise omission and explicit `legacy`, and explicit `approved`; each preview checks both its pinned source and proposed result with that one profile. # Summary

Define Plan decomposition Relations

## Scope

Plan-decomposition Relations in the Plan Graph.

## Claim

**in** the Plan Graph, `A DECOMPOSES_INTO B` **means** that completing Plan `B` contributes required work **to** completing Plan `A`; `B IS_DECOMPOSITION_OF A` is the inverse view of the same fact.

- the source **and** target are distinct Plan Atoms, independently of their Labels.
- decomposition is an all-of relation: **all** decomposed Plans are required for completion under CA-R-1583.
- decomposition concerns planned work, **not** Claim containment, Scope Unit parentage, **or** Type inheritance.
- the decomposing Plan owns the direct `IS_DECOMPOSITION_OF` declaration under CA-D-481; derive `DECOMPOSES_INTO` from that same fact, **not** from folder placement.

## Details

### relation admission

- owning graph kind: Plan Graph under CA-R-1593; endpoints are Plan Atom references **in** that graph, **not** native nodes of a different graph.
- Status: the Relation Kind is Active; endpoint Plan Revisions use the admitted Plan Status model, **without** requiring every historical **or** pending endpoint **to** be Active.
- authority effect: retain the existing endpoint identities, Claims, Scope Units, **and** tiers; this Relation does **not** transfer authority.
- cardinality: **`<=1`** authored `IS_DECOMPOSITION_OF` target **and** **`>=0`** derived `DECOMPOSES_INTO` targets per Plan.
- transitivity: the direct Relation is **not** transitively materialized; recursive reachability is derived under CA-R-1537.

# Summary

Define Plan blocking

## Scope

Plan-blocking Relations in the Plan Graph.

## Claim

**in** the Plan Graph, `A BLOCKS B` **means** that Plan `B` **may** start **only** **after** Plan `A` is Done.

- a Plan **may** block **>=0** other Plans **and** have **>=0** blockers.
- **all** blockers **must** be Done **before** the blocked work starts.
- navigation order, a shared Hub, **and** `DECOMPOSES_INTO` do **not** establish `BLOCKS`.
- an inverse lookup is derived from the same explicit fact, **not** separately authored; Subject DEPENDS_ON remains a different Relation Kind.

## Details

### relation admission

- owning graph kind: Plan Graph under CA-R-1593; endpoints are Plan Atom references **in** that graph, **not** native nodes of a different graph.
- Status: the Relation Kind is Active; endpoint Plan Revisions use the admitted Plan Status model, **without** requiring every historical **or** pending endpoint **to** be Active.
- authority effect: retain the existing endpoint identities, Claims, Scope Units, **and** tiers; this Relation does **not** transfer authority.
- cardinality: **>=0** distinct direct targets **and** **>=0** distinct incoming blockers; inverse direction is blocked Plan **to** blocker.
- transitivity: retain **only** explicit direct edges; prerequisite reachability **may** be derived for readiness **and** cycle checks **without** creating authored transitive edges.

# Summary

Classify admitted Atom changes by semantic effect

## Scope

the classification of admitted Atom changes by semantic effect.

## Claim

**before** changing an admitted Atom, CAPRMEDIO **must** assign **`=1`** change class using these boundaries, identity results, **and** required reviews:

| Change class | Boundary | Identity result | Required review |
|---|---|---|---|
| `carrier_only` | Representation, the Atom's own filename **or** local placement, encoding, **or** lossless Entity-name/reference renaming **without** changing governed meaning **or** the Atom's Summary value | Keep the Atom ID; increment Version by exactly **`1`** | Verify lossless recoding |
| `refinement` | Wording **or** criteria become clearer **or** stricter while primary Claim, applicability, **and** acceptance meaning remain equivalent **and** the Summary value remains unchanged | Keep the Atom ID; increment Version by exactly **`1`** | Demonstrate equivalence |
| `semantic_revision` | Meaning **or** applicability changes while the same primary Claim remains recognizable **and** the Summary value remains unchanged | Keep the Atom ID; increment Version by exactly **`1`** **and** create a new Revision | Declare the delta **and** complete lineage-impact review |
| `replacement` | the Summary value changes under CA-R-1464, the primary Claim changes identity, **or** an independently replaceable Claim is added **or** removed | Create a new Atom ID; preserve the predecessor **and** successor identity binding under CA-R-807 | Review the replacement boundary **and** affected lineage |

**if** Scope narrowing **or** expansion preserves the primary Claim identity **and** Summary value, **then** it is a `semantic_revision`, **not** a carrier-only change. splitting **or** combining independently replaceable Claims is a `replacement`. the Summary-change replacement rule takes precedence even **when** the Claim remains unchanged; lossless serialization of the same Summary value is **not** a Summary change. the semantic change class is independent of storage transactions **or** version-control change sets; persistence preserves the admitted Atom, Carrier, **and** Journal authority.

**every** actual same-ID update **must** increment Version by exactly **`1`**, regardless of change class, **and** refresh Updated At under CA-R-1788. an exact no-op **must** retain Version **and** Updated At. retaining the predecessor as history **must** preserve its exact prior bytes, including its prior Version, Status **and** Updated At; retaining history is **not** another edit to that predecessor.

this classification concerns changes **to** the Atom's own bytes, metadata, direct ownership **or** local placement. moving an ancestor **only** changes a descendant's repository locator **when** that descendant's own bytes, metadata, direct owner **and** placement relative **to** that owner remain unchanged; this is **not** an Atom update **and** **must** retain that descendant's Version **and** Updated At. this boundary applies **to** **all** Atoms, including Plans nested under a moved Plan **and** Atoms whose owning Scope Unit moves. an actual change **to** the Atom itself, including its Status, filename, direct owner **or** local placement, still follows the classification **and** revision rules above. exact older Revision bytes remain unchanged.

Tools **may** propose a class but **must** fail closed **when** the distinction between refinement, semantic revision, **and** replacement is uncertain.

# Summary

Classify admitted Atom changes by semantic effect

## Scope

the classification of admitted Atom changes by semantic effect.

## Claim

**before** changing an admitted Atom, CAPRMEDIO **must** assign **`=1`** change class using these boundaries, identity results, **and** required reviews:

| Change class | Boundary | Identity result | Required review |
|---|---|---|---|
| `carrier_only` | Representation, the Atom's own filename **or** local placement, encoding, **or** lossless Entity-name/reference renaming **without** changing governed meaning **or** the Atom's Summary value | Keep the Atom ID; increment Version by exactly **`1`** | Verify lossless recoding |
| `refinement` | Wording **or** criteria become clearer **or** stricter while primary Claim, applicability, **and** acceptance meaning remain equivalent **and** the Summary value remains unchanged | Keep the Atom ID; increment Version by exactly **`1`** | Demonstrate equivalence |
| `semantic_revision` | Meaning **or** applicability changes while the same primary Claim remains recognizable **and** the Summary value remains unchanged | Keep the Atom ID; increment Version by exactly **`1`** **and** create a new Revision | Declare the delta **and** complete lineage-impact review |
| `replacement` | the Summary value changes under CA-R-1464, the primary Claim changes identity, **or** an independently replaceable Claim is added **or** removed | Create a new Atom ID; preserve the predecessor **and** successor identity binding under CA-R-807 | Review the replacement boundary **and** affected lineage |

**if** Scope narrowing **or** expansion preserves the primary Claim identity **and** Summary value, **then** it is a `semantic_revision`, **not** a carrier-only change. splitting **or** combining independently replaceable Claims is a `replacement`. the Summary-change replacement rule takes precedence even **when** the Claim remains unchanged; lossless serialization of the same Summary value is **not** a Summary change. the semantic change class is independent of storage transactions **or** version-control change sets; persistence preserves the admitted Atom, Carrier, **and** Journal authority.

**every** actual same-ID update **must** increment Version by exactly **`1`**, regardless of change class, **and** refresh Updated At under CA-R-1788. an exact no-op **must** retain Version **and** Updated At. retaining the predecessor as history **must** preserve its exact prior bytes, including its prior Version, Status **and** Updated At; retaining history is **not** another edit to that predecessor.

this classification concerns changes **to** the Atom's own bytes, metadata, direct ownership **or** local placement. moving an ancestor **only** changes a descendant's repository locator **when** that descendant's own bytes, metadata, direct owner **and** placement relative **to** that owner remain unchanged; this is **not** an Atom update **and** **must** retain that descendant's Version **and** Updated At. this boundary applies **to** **all** Atoms, including Plans nested under a moved Plan **and** Atoms whose owning Scope Unit moves. an actual change **to** the Atom itself, including its Status, filename, direct owner **or** local placement, still follows the classification **and** revision rules above. exact older Revision bytes remain unchanged.

Tools **may** propose a class but **must** fail closed **when** the distinction between refinement, semantic revision, **and** replacement is uncertain.

# Summary

Resolve lifecycle changes from applicable Status models

## Scope

Workflows that change an Entity's Status.

## Claim

a Workflow for changing an Entity's Status **must** admit **any** requested Status allowed by that Entity's applicable status model, rather than a fixed list built into the Workflow. For Atom creation **and** explicit Atom Status updates, **any** value admitted by the qualified Content Role/Type model is selectable **without** a required intermediate Status **or** transition matrix.

## Details

- resolve the model using the actual Entity kind **and**, for an Atom, its qualified Content Role **and** Type.
- apply the same model-driven rule **to** a Scope Unit **or** Atom Collection **when** a status model is defined for it.
- preserve authorization, expected-source/currentness, identity/collision, schema **and** applicable Carrier rules; support for **any** admitted Atom Status does **not** authorize arbitrary values **or** unrelated effects. Non-Atom Entity models retain their own applicable transition conditions.
- **every** admitted Status change of a folder-backed Plan, Workflow, **or** Step parent requires the same requested Status for **all** recursively contained Plan **or** Operations descendants, for **every** admitted target Status, **not** only Archived. containment selects the descendants; references **to** Atoms outside that Carrier tree do **not** select them.
- compose separate independently admitted single-Atom Actions for the parent **and** each selected descendant. each Action checks its own qualified Status model **and** ordinary effect preconditions; an unsupported value is a refusal for that Atom, **not** an invented Status **or** a multi-target Action. this rule does **not** establish an atomic batch **or** rollback transaction.
- select **only** the latest Revision of each affected Atom. retain exact prior Revision bytes, including Version, Status **and** Updated At; an older archived Revision is **not** a cascade target. applicable placement keeps descendants inside the parent Carrier tree, including **when** Archived.
- a cascade is an authoring operation that writes each affected Atom's own admitted Status **and** Revision metadata. reading a containing folder **or** parent Status **must not** infer **or** override a descendant's carried Status.
- changing the admitted values **within** the supported model **must not** require a separate Workflow for **every** value. unsupported model capabilities **must** be reported rather than silently approximated.
- a missing status model **must not** be replaced with an invented universal Draft, Active, **or** Archived lifecycle for **all** Artifacts **and** Structural Entities.

# Summary

Use Economical YAML Frontmatter

## Scope

YAML Frontmatter of Markdown Atom Carriers.

## Claim

the YAML Frontmatter of a Markdown Atom Carrier **must** use the least syntax **and** nesting that preserves unambiguous deterministic parsing, validation, extensibility, **and** human readability.

## Details

### Common field encoding

use the following field encodings for the applicable Atom Properties. presence follows the cited Property authority, **not** observed filename tokens. a String is a nonempty YAML string; an Integer excludes Booleans. a null value does **not** satisfy a required Property.

| Property | Top-level field | Encoding **and** applicable presence |
|---|---|---|
| Atom Identity | `atom_id` | String under CA-D-446; forbidden for ordinary Draft, required for non-Draft; its explicit Subjects-only edit-draft exception carries only the temporary canonical-ID-plus-`@draft` proposal marker; carry Version separately |
| Content Role | `content_role` | **=1** String selecting its canonical Content Role; resolve the admitted domain from applicable authority |
| Type | `type` | **=1** String selecting an admitted specialized Type **when** one applies; omit for an ordinary Requirement, Method, **or** Delivery Atom under CA-R-1700; other Content Roles retain their applicable Type requirements; a present field **must not** be null, empty, **or** a collection; filename Type tokens are **not** a second value |
| current Scope Unit **or** external Atom Author | `current_scope_unit` | **=1** String: the registered Scope Unit Name, **or**, for an Atom outside **every** Scope Unit, its Author's registered Operator name, exactly equal **to** the carried `author` value |
| Claim Target Scope Unit | `claim_target_scope_unit` | use CA-D-482 |
| Local Tier | `local_tier` | String under CA-R-155; omit for a Project Goal under CA-R-1393; otherwise carry the selected canonical tier explicitly, including Standard |
| Global Tier | `global_tier` | **=1** Integer under CA-R-1413, including an admitted negative value; verify against applicable tier authority **without** substituting a filename-derived value |
| Version **and** Updated At | `version`, `updated_at` | use CA-D-270 |
| Author | `author` | use CA-D-274 |
| Status | `status` | use CA-D-483 |
| Subjects | `subjects` | use CA-D-269; **only** the governed Subject keys **and** their admitted encodings |
| authored Atom Relations | `relations` | use CA-D-268; omission **or** an empty mapping represents no authored Relations; **every** present Relation Kind carries its nonempty target collection |

- `current_scope_unit` **must not** be null, a list, a joined set of names, **or** replaced by an `operators` field. the external Author fallback does **not** make the Author a Scope Unit **or** create an Actor owner of the Atom. resolve the permitted reference kind from the applicable Atom model **and** registered identities. a failed Scope Unit resolution does **not** prove the Atom is outside **every** Scope Unit. never infer the value from its filename.
- the Revision Identifier is composed from `atom_id` **and** `version` under CA-D-446; do **not** duplicate it **in** an `identifier` field. an ordinary Draft has Version **and** Updated At but no assigned Atom ID. CA-D-446's explicitly source-pinned Subjects-only edit draft carries a temporary proposal marker, never an assigned canonical ID.
- Summary **and** Claim use their body sections under CA-D-479, **not** `summary` **or** `claim` frontmatter copies. other body Properties use their own registered section authority.

### Conditional fields and expansion

- a Plan's explicit `assignee` uses **<=1** String identifying an admitted Actor under CA-D-473. `autonomous_confidence_threshold` **and** `implementation_retry_limit` use their integer encodings under CA-D-472 **and** CA-D-447. inherited values remain omitted unless explicitly selected; self-sufficiency does **not** copy them.
- `priority` follows CA-D-386 for Concern Atoms **only**. additional Plan, Operations, proof, **or** other Type-specific fields require their applicable Delivery declarations; their occurrence **in** old Carriers does **not** admit them.
- the generated `projection` block is admitted **only** **in** a projected representation under CA-D-305, with **only** its defined `source_carrier_path` String. it is **not** an authored source Atom Property.
- a new field **or** nested key requires applicable authority that settles its canonical location, value type, cardinality, admission condition, **and** permitted values **or** reference resolution. unadmitted fields are invalid; an admitted Property with an unsettled encoding is a schema gap, **not** permission **to** guess **or** report full conformance.
- apply explicitly governed migration exceptions **only** within their declared boundary. legacy presence alone is **not** an exception; retired fields under CA-D-478 remain rejected.

### Subjects-only edit-draft exception

CA-D-446's explicit source-pinned Subjects-only edit draft is a derived proposed next Revision of an existing Atom, not a new Atom Draft or another canonical original. It may carry the temporary `atom_id: <canonical-ID>@draft`, `status: Draft`, and matching temporary-ID filename in the owning role's `draft/` folder while the exact canonical source remains untouched. The reviewed packet retains the canonical target/source pin and exact draft path/digest for that specific proposed edit. Approval restores the canonical ID and original Status, independently validates normalized Subjects-only materialization, and uses the existing exact predecessor archive plus N+1/actual-time update. Staging and publication require no retained Draft-history entry, `revision_lineage`, unique Draft head, origin chain or consuming successor. New-Atom Drafts and ordinary lifecycle Drafts remain ID-free; canonical ID grammar and the normal source, schema, identity/collision, permission and exact actual-history safeguards are unchanged.

# Summary

Give Every Non-Draft Atom Revision One Identifier

## Scope

non-Draft Atom Revisions and Draft Carriers.

## Claim

**every** non-Draft Atom Revision **must** have **`=1`** Identifier composed from its Atom Identity **and** Version.

- carry the assigned Atom Identity as the top-level String `atom_id` **and** Version as `version`; their pair identifies this Revision **without** another `identifier` field.
- outside the explicit Subjects-only edit-draft exception below, a Draft Carrier **must not** carry an assigned `atom_id`; a filename, path, **or** temporary locator **must not** silently allocate one.
- when an identified Atom is changed to Draft, remove `atom_id` from the resulting Draft Carrier's complete frontmatter **and** its assigned filename number under CA-D-288-CORE_META_MODEL-DELIVERY--serialize-draft-atom-filenames-with-an-empty-number; do **not** create a second concurrent Draft Carrier for that Status edit.
- preserve the exact prior identified Revision as history, including its old Version, Status and Updated At. An actual Status edit, including demotion to Draft, advances the current Version from N to N+1 with actual edit time under CA-R-1432/CA-R-1788; an exact no-op retains Version/time. There is no demotion Version exception.
- every ID-free Draft later leaving Draft receives a fresh next-unreused Atom Identity under CA-D-508, even when a Tool previously demoted it. Historical identity/lineage is retained as fact, not restored as that Draft's assigned ID or released for reuse.

## Details

### Subjects-only edit draft of an existing Atom

A Subjects-only edit draft of an existing identified Atom is a derived proposal for that Atom's next Revision, not another canonical original, a new Atom Draft, or a demotion of the current Revision. It is admitted only with an explicit canonical target and exact current ID/Version/SHA-256 source pin retained by the reviewed batch packet. The canonical current Carrier remains untouched during staging. This narrowly scoped proposal carries `atom_id` equal to the canonical ID plus the exact suffix `@draft` and `status: Draft`; that temporary proposal ID is not an assigned canonical Atom Identity, a new Type, or a globally valid canonical ID/reference syntax.

Its filename replaces the source's canonical ID once with that temporary proposal ID in the owning role's `draft/` folder. Bind the complete proposed bytes and safe path/digest to the reviewed packet. Apart from the declared Subjects, temporary ID/Status and proposed Version/time, preserve the source's complete metadata and body bytes. A changed proposal shows N+1 and illustrative Updated At; a true no-op retains the source Version/time behind its temporary proposal markers.

Approval rechecks the exact canonical source-before and reviewed draft bytes. Normalize only the temporary ID and Draft marker back to the pinned canonical ID and original Status, and materialize actual Updated At for a changed update. Require equality with independently validated fresh Subjects-only canonical materialization before the existing updater archives the exact current predecessor and publishes N+1. Preserve original Status and every other unrelated byte; do not allocate identity, perform a lifecycle Status transition, infer identity from a suffix alone, or bypass current source validation. A changed source or proposal refuses rather than silently rebinding approval. Existing low-level effect/restoration handling remains.

New-Atom Drafts and ordinary lifecycle Draft demotion/update/identification retain their ID-free filename and applicable identity rules, without a retained Draft-history entry, lineage/head/origin chain or consuming-successor prerequisite under CA-D-568/CA-D-570. Removing those prerequisites does not waive schema, identity/collision, expected-target/currentness, permission or exact actual-history safeguards. This exception supplies no general assigned-ID Draft admission and does not change canonical Atom ID grammar.

# Summary

Assess source conflicts

## Operation

Assess Source Conflicts **means** the reusable Action that assesses one exact selected source frontier against its applicable authority **and** returns the conflict assessment **without** changing sources.

1. load the current accepted active authority **and** applicable Project Principles **before** relying on an earlier report **or** proposed fix.
2. identify the conflicting Claims **and** their applicability. for RMEDO Atoms, collect Global Tier, exact Revision, **and** Updated At. distinguish an actual conflict from different permitted cases.
3. for RMEDO conflicts, preserve higher-tier authority, whose Global Tier number is lower. within the applicable authority boundaries, prefer the freshest accepted active Claim over a conflicting older Claim; Updated At **must not** permit a lower-tier Claim **or** prohibited source override **to** defeat higher-tier authority.
4. check **every** proposed disposition against the active Principles **and** retain the evidence for its effect on alignment. a conflict between active Principles requires the Operator under CA-R-1551.
5. distinguish resolved, unresolved, **and** unevaluated conditions. report missing checks, uncertain applicability, equal **or** ambiguous timestamps, **and** unresolved authority **without** inventing precedence.
6. verify required resolution evidence against the exact proposal **and** current source frontier. missing, stale, partial, ambiguous, **or** mismatched approval **or** delegation does **not** resolve a conflict.

7. check affected authority coverage, including still-required Claims, active references **and** Relations, **and** required Evaluations. report an unresolved gap separately from a resolved conflict; absence of a conflict does **not** prove complete coverage.

this Action **must not** synthesize **or** merge Claims, treat an LLM judgment as Operator authorization, change source **or** projected content, **or** silently exclude a conflicting source from the assessment.

# Summary

Propose source corrections

## Operation

Propose Source Corrections **means** the reusable Action that prepares an explicit correction for an identified conflict **in** one exact selected source frontier.

1. use the current assessment from CA-O-005, including Global Tier, Updated At, **and** Principle alignment. identify the affected source authority, exact proposed change, intended outcome, effects, **and** uncertainty.
2. consider archiving a conflicting Atom **when** removing its active authority improves alignment with the Principles. do **not** retain an obsolete Atom merely because it already exists.
3. **before** proposing archival, account for **every** still-required Claim **and** affected reference, Relation, Evaluation, **and** dependent authority. identify its remaining active owner **or** the exact prerequisite repair; do **not** invent a successor for a Claim that governing authority explicitly withdraws.
4. leave no gap **in** the affected authority: missing coverage, dangling active references, lost required checks, **or** an unresolved conflict blocks completion. required replacement **or** absorption successors **must** be Active **before** the predecessor is archived. unique valid content **must** be preserved **before** removing the mixed Atom.
5. target corrections **only** at their owning source through its governed change workflow, **not** at a derived copy. preserve the exact archival history **and** record replacement **or** absorption under CA-R-807.
6. return the proposal **and** its authorization needs. **if** no sufficiently supported gap-free correction fits the applicable authority **and** confidence constraints, report the exact uncertainty for Operator escalation.

a proposal does **not** authorize **or** perform the change. no duplicate authority **must** be created merely **to** make archival possible.

## Operation

Apply Approved Source Corrections **means** the reusable Action that applies **only** the exact upstream corrections authorized for the current proposal, conflict, **and** source frontier.

2. apply the authorized correction through the owning source's governed change workflow. resulting Claims remain **in** their owning source Atoms; resulting selections remain **in** their owning settings. compilation **and** an approval record do **not** themselves grant source-change authority.
3. for archival, verify CA-O-006's coverage conditions against live sources, complete prerequisite repairs, **and** preserve the predecessor under CA-O-051: retain its exact prior Revision bytes as history **without** changing prior Version, Status **or** Updated At; retain the current predecessor's body, Summary, identity **and** all metadata except Version, archived Status **and** archive-time Updated At, incrementing Version by exactly **`1`** for that actual update. apply replacement **or** absorption recording under CA-R-807 **when** applicable; a withdrawn obsolete Claim does **not** require an invented successor.
4. record actual execution, changes, failures, **and** partial effects **in** the Journal. report the resulting source frontier **or** exact failure; a Journal record describes those effects **without** replacing current source authority.
5. return changed sources for renewed selection, conflict assessment, Principle alignment, **and** affected coverage checks. do **not** report completion **until** required checks confirm no remaining conflict **or** coverage gap **in** the affected authority.

this Action **must not** edit projected Claims as a conflict fix, infer additional corrections, create a duplicate approval Atom, **or** claim completion **after** a failed correction. retries **and** recovery require their applicable accepted authority **and** bounds; this Action does **not** authorize automatic rollback **or** unbounded repetition.

# Summary

Publish the Applicable Methodology

## Operation

this Step is the publish node **of** CA-O-011, Applicable Methodology Compilation, invoking **`=1`** Action, CA-O-009, Publish Reconciled Projection.

### Inputs and parameters

bind the final reassessed source frontier from CA-O-153, the corresponding selection from CA-O-152, required valid decisions from CA-O-155 when applicable, and the Workflow Run's selected Projection Delivery authority.

preserve **every** selected Atom ID, exact source Revision, authority owner, **and** Claim under CA-R-1314 **and** CA-R-1316; enforce CA-R-1461 **and** CA-D-305 **and** CA-D-306 source identity, exact source Carrier bytes **and** Carrier form. fail **without** changing Applicable Methodology membership **if** **any** conflict remains unresolved **or** **any** required approval is invalid. produce the same ordered Applicable Methodology membership from the same resolved source frontier.

# Summary

Prepare structural change

## Operation

Prepare Structural Change **means** the Action that produces one bounded change proposal against the exact current Project Structure state. the proposal identifies the requested creation, rename, reparenting, reorder, path rebinding, removal, **or** reconciliation; its expected declarations; affected references, Goals, descendants **and** Carriers; required source changes; validation conditions; **and** a recoverable cutover boundary. a rename **or** reparenting **must** account for incoming references **and** parent-owned Goals, rather than leaving them attached **to** a different unit. declaration removal **must not** imply Carrier deletion. an undeclared folder, missing folder, **or** missing Active Goal is an observation requiring an explicit disposition, **not** permission **to** invent, erase, **or** accept authority.

# Summary

Authorize structural change

## Operation

Authorize Structural Change **means** the Action that checks a structural change proposal against the Operator's actual authorization **and** the effective Autonomous Confidence Threshold, returning permission for the exact proposed effects **or** a blocked decision with its reason. existing authorization **may** cover those effects; a new approval **must** be requested **if** they exceed it, conflict resolution requires it, **or** uncertainty fails the effective threshold. approval **must** remain bound **to** the proposal **and** selected source state. this Action **must not** infer permission from a folder observation, a generated result, confidence alone, **or** the existence of a Plan.

Apply structural change

## Operation

## Operation

Implementation Workflow **means** the test-first implementation graph below; its referenced Step Atoms own Action/input/context bindings, **and** its Action Atoms own operational behavior.

- entry: CA-O-091.
- nodes: CA-O-091, CA-O-092, CA-O-093, CA-O-094, CA-O-095, CA-O-096, CA-O-099.
- transitions between Steps use Workflow-scoped `ON_RESULT`; `completed` **and** `blocked` are terminal results, **not** Steps.

| From Step | Result condition | Next Step **or** terminal result |
|---|---|---|
| CA-O-091 | evaluation_ready | CA-O-092 |
| CA-O-091 | requirement_ready | CA-O-093 |
| CA-O-091 | evaluation_runnable | CA-O-094 |

| CA-O-095 | unresolved | blocked |

a terminal blocker preserves completed effects **and** pending P work. resumption requires fresh admission under the definition-binding rules; it is **not** success **or** permission **to** silently replay completed work.

Method creation **and** acceptance are outside this Workflow. return retained issue, test, diagnosis, **and** fix evidence for a separately invoked Method-learning Run under CA-O-102; neither that Run nor creation of an M Atom is an implementation-completion prerequisite.

# Summary

Prepare implementation work

## Operation

Implementation Preparation **means** the Agentic Action that resolves an implementation request into persistent Plan work **and** the next prerequisite-ready item.

### Inputs and authority preparation

- receive the bounded implementation request, an existing P/Plan Atom **when** supplied, admitted authority sources **and** their declared input universe, the selected implementation mode, complete execution inputs, retained work, candidate-specific evidence, **and** applicable permissions.
- gather the selected active Requirement **and** Delivery Atoms as what **to** implement: required behavior, constraints, Carriers, **and** delivery boundaries. gather applicable Evaluation Atoms separately as check authority; retain test-first work rather than dropping E from the Run.
- compile **all** active Method Atoms **in** the declared input universe into **=1** file **before** delegated implementation work. preserve full frontmatter **and** Markdown content, source identity, Revision, path, **and** digest for **every** included Atom; do **not** replace Claims with summaries **or** silently omit Methods. a supplied compiled file **may** be reused **only** after these checks.
- bind the declared input universe **and** compare file membership with the complete active Method inventory. order entries by Atom ID **and** Revision for repeatability, **not** as new priority. stale sources, conflicting source identities, missing content, **or** unverifiable completeness return `blocked`.
- the compiled file is a derived input Projection, **not** a second source of Method authority. apply **all** Methods governing the selected work **without** treating unrelated Methods as applicable merely because they are present. pass the same verified file binding **to** downstream Steps; an authorized authority change requires refreshed inputs.
- include applicable higher-tier authority, current Project Principles, concrete input/output boundaries, **and** test commands **or** enough admitted information **to** establish them. incomplete **or** conflicting authority returns `blocked`, **not** guessed scope.

### Plan preparation and selection

- reuse the supplied Plan **and** existing suitable decomposition. **when** no Plan was supplied, create the admitted P/Plan for the bounded request **before** code work starts. Tasks **and** subtasks are P/Plan Atoms with their own Claims, Assignees, **and** Definitions of Done, **not** Workflow Steps **or** an ephemeral checklist.
- **when** practical, decompose work into independently verifiable P Atoms with an ETA **<15** minutes for one assigned AI Agent. record the estimate **and** its assumptions **in** Plan Details; it is an estimate, **not** an automatic time limit. **if** safe decomposition cannot meet the applicable leaf-work bound, return the specific blocker rather than inventing small estimates **or** weakening the Definition of Done.
- store `IS_DECOMPOSITION_OF` **only** on the child Plan **and** actual start prerequisites through `BLOCKS`, following CA-M-306 **and** CA-D-481. preserve an acyclic combined completion graph under CA-R-1592. navigation order is **not** a dependency.
- select **=1** ready bounded Plan item **and** its assigned subagent context for test, implementation, diagnosis, **and** repair work. provide source-bound inputs, owned files/work boundary, expected outputs, verification, relevant prior results, **and** effective confidence/retry gates; preserve unrelated work.
- derive prerequisite-first work order under CA-M-239. prepare tests **before** the behavior they check wherever actual prerequisites permit; execute the prepared baseline tests **before** implementing that behavior **when** runnable. minimum execution prerequisites are explicit, **not** permission **to** implement the entire feature first. use Atom ID **only** **to** break remaining ties between ready work items.
- unchanged implementation mode, governing RMED, **and** complete execution inputs **must** yield the same applicable work **and** prerequisite-respecting order. retained results determine residual work, **not** a different normative interpretation.
- retain completed work **and** candidate-specific evidence. a new Method activation **or** other authorized authority change requires refreshed Projection inputs **and** renewed work/Evaluation resolution; it does **not** erase prior effects **or** reset retry accounting.

### Results and execution boundary

- return `evaluation_ready`, `requirement_ready`, **or** `evaluation_runnable` with the selected Plan, exact work, prerequisites, assigned context, current baseline, gathered R/D targets, the compiled Method file binding, **and** separate Evaluation authority.
- return `complete` **only** after **all** selected implementation Plan work, required child Plans, Definitions of Done, **and** applicable Evaluations are satisfied, with no failed, blocked, stale, **or** unevaluated implementation obligations. return retained issue/diagnosis/fix evidence for separate Method learning; creating **or** accepting a Method is **not** a completion condition **or** a next Step **in** this Run.
- return `blocked` for unmet authority, capability, confidence, permission, prerequisite, **or** Plan admission, including nonempty residual work with no ready next item.
- current execution uses the host's native subagent, file, **and** command capabilities. MCP **or** a running Workflow server is **not** required. missing subagent capability blocks delegated work rather than silently executing it **in** the main session. Step bindings own the Integrated/Isolated choice; do **not** introduce a Workflow-wide context Property.

## Operation

Evaluation Implementation **means** the Agentic Action that prepares **or** reuses the tests for selected implementation work **before** its required behavior is implemented.

- inputs: the selected P/Plan item, active Method Projection, applicable R/E/D authority, current candidate, existing tests, complete test inputs, **and** owned work boundary.

- honor the selection procedure established by applicable Methods **and** the acceptance, priority, **and** disposition rules established by applicable Evaluation authority. prepare the complete admitted portfolio at its selected observable boundaries; no test scope has default priority. preserve issue-driven targeted checks as complementary evidence **without** creating Method Atoms.

# Summary

Repair nonconforming Implementation

## Operation

Implementation Repair **means** the Agentic Action that repairs a diagnosed code defect within the admitted work boundary **and** retry allowance, preserving the issue **and** verification evidence.

- inputs: the diagnosed implementation **or** test-implementation defect, failed candidate, governing R/E/D, active Method Projection, selected P/Plan item, verification commands, retained issue evidence, **and** an admitted fix-and-evaluate retry.
- require evidence sufficient **to** explain the cause **and** correction. unresolved diagnosis, conflicting authority, unmet confidence, **or** missing permission returns `blocked`; retry allowance grants no extra authority.
- reproduce the issue with an appropriate targeted test **before** the fix **when** possible. reuse an existing reproducer; add unit, integration, **or** another focused test according **to** governing Methods. distinguish the actual defect from a setup failure.
- correct the code under existing authority **and** permissions. test code is Implementation too; do **not** weaken an Evaluation, expected output, Requirement, **or** Delivery obligation **to** obtain a pass.
- return `repaired` with the changed candidate, failure evidence, diagnosis, actual correction, tests, expected outcomes, **and** replay commands for re-evaluation. passing targeted checks do **not** replace any other check retained **in** the admitted Evaluation portfolio.
- do **not** create, update, **or** promote corrective M Atoms **in** this Action. retain evidence for the separate Method-learning Workflow; learning is **not** a condition for accepting a verified implementation fix.
- return `authority_change_required` **if** a governing RMED change is necessary, for disposition under CA-R-1559 **before** changing that authority. authorized baseline changes require renewed preparation; do **not** reset retry accounting.

# Summary

Control implementation retries

## Operation

Implementation Retry Control **means** the Agentic Action that determines whether the next fix-and-evaluate retry **may** start within the current Implementation Workflow Run's retry allowance **and** governing permissions. repair **and** re-evaluation remain Actions **in** the Implementation Workflow under CA-O-016.

### Execution

1. resolve the effective Implementation Retry Limit under CA-M-295. **if** resolution fails, stop the retry decision **and** request Operator disposition.
2. **if** successful completion under CA-O-016 has been reached, stop **without** permitting another automatic repair retry.
3. **before** permitting a retry, check the applicable confidence threshold under CA-R-1591, governing-Atom approval rules under CA-R-1559, **and** **all** additional Operator constraints. an unmet gate requires the applicable earlier escalation even **when** retries remain; retry allowance does **not** create permission.
4. **if** failure remains **and** the consumed retry count has reached the effective Implementation Retry Limit, pause **and** report the remaining failures **to** the Operator.
5. **only** **when** failure remains, the gates permit recovery, **and** a retry remains, permit the next fix-and-evaluate retry through CA-O-016.

### Accounting

- the initial failed Evaluation consumes **`=0`** retries.
- count **`=1`** retry **when** a permitted fix-and-evaluate round starts, **not** merely **when** its permission is checked. repeated gate checks **must not** double-count that round.
- retain the consumed count throughout the current Workflow Run; another Step Run does **not** begin a new retry budget. a changed failure set **or** an automatic next loop **must not** silently reset the budget.

# Summary

Review and repair a bounded RMED Atom batch

## Operation

RMED Atom Review Workflow **means** the graph with these **`=3`** Steps:

1. gather the requested scope of active RMED Atoms through CA-O-108.
2. check the selected Atoms through CA-O-109.
3. fix confirmed issues through CA-O-110.

each main Step has **`=1`** result-coverage substep invoking CA-O-118: CA-O-119 **after** gather, CA-O-120 **after** check, CA-O-121 **after** fix. these Coverage Gates inspect execution evidence, **not** Atom correctness. **only** coverage **`=100`** percent permits the next main Step **or** completion; incomplete **or** unknown coverage interrupts the Run **and** asks the Operator with the missing work. no automatic repair retry **or** reduced selection follows a failed gate.

| From Step | Result condition | Next Step **or** terminal result |
|---|---|---|
| CA-O-108 | ready | CA-O-109 |
| CA-O-108 | empty | completed |
| CA-O-108 | blocked | blocked |
| CA-O-109 | checked_clean | completed |
| CA-O-109 | issues | CA-O-110 |
| CA-O-109 | blocked | blocked |
| CA-O-110 | fixed_not_rechecked | completed |
| CA-O-110 | replaced_not_rechecked | completed |
| CA-O-110 | blocked | blocked |

the review profile is `atom_local`: **`=1`** Scope, **`=1`** Claim with faithful Summary **and** explanatory Details, intact carried Properties, **and** current CCE alignment. Entity-model correction, Subject completeness, relation-target resolution, duplicate detection, **and** cross-Atom alignment are outside this Run.

## Details

the caller gives **`=1`** Atom **to** a fresh Isolated reviewer. independent assignments **may** run **in** parallel. supply the actual Atom **and** the relevant local checking rules; keep **`=1`** report per Atom **and** **`=1`** progress list for the original selection.

this Workflow has no proposal-review stage, saved-Atom recheck, **or** fix-and-recheck loop. Coverage Gates review the completeness of saved execution evidence **only**. `checked_clean` records a passing check; `fixed_not_rechecked` records applied corrections **without** asserting a post-fix pass. another review requires a separately requested Run.

continue **until** the original selection is handled **or** a genuine blocker requires the Operator:

- at the configured context threshold, save a short handoff naming the current Atom, unfinished Step, completed edits, **and** next work; automatically continue **in** a fresh subagent.
- preserve completed work **and** resume **only** unfinished work. a context handoff consumes no repair retry.
- **when** slots are occupied, wait for a worker **to** finish. retain actual spawn failures **and** unresolved permission **or** confidence questions as blockers.
- a completed subset does **not** complete the original selection.

completion requires **all** **`=6`** initial checks **to** conclude **and** **all** confirmed findings **to** be corrected **or** rejected with recorded reasons. an applied edit does **not** complete an unfinished check. count reports received, check completion, **and** Atom completion separately; unresolved coverage **or** findings keep the Atom **and** Run incomplete. independent Atoms **may** progress from checking **to** fixing **in** parallel.

### Replacement permission

- `allow_replacements` defaults **to** `false`. a caller **may** set it **to** `true` **with** fix permission **to** delegate Summary-changing replacement of selected Atoms.
- an admitted replacement receives a new Atom ID **and** Version **`=1`**; archive the predecessor **and** record **both** Carrier bindings **and** the replacement **in** the shared Journal **and** Run report.
- return `replaced_not_rechecked` for an applied replacement; this result asserts completed correction, **not** a post-fix semantic pass. changing other Atoms remains outside this local Run.

### Run evidence

- at the start of an Operator-authorized Run, bind its Workflow name, Run ID, full report location, **and** shared Project Journal. retain the same Run ID through **all** Steps **and** context handoffs.
