# Summary

Manage atom lifecycle

## Operation

One reusable parameterized Workflow graph binds Create Atom, Update Atom, Replace Atom and Change Atom Status. Archive is only a Change Status shortcut admitted by the applicable model, not another Workflow. The Step definitions own all Action and input bindings.

Each invocation admits exactly one Create target or one existing current target/predecessor, with its complete required Carrier set. Replace retains the complete accepted set of >=1 distinct successors for that one predecessor, not additional predecessors. A request naming multiple independent targets/predecessors ends blocked before Step dispatch or effects; bulk callers expand their requests into separate individually admitted Runs of this same Workflow, with fresh exact inputs/assessment/permission bindings for each.

For a containment cascade required by R1521, the calling Workflow binds the parent and every selected contained Plan or Operations Atom's latest Revision as separate individually admitted Runs of this Workflow, all requesting the same Status under each target's own model. Older historical Revisions and references outside the parent Carrier tree are excluded. Each Run retains the single-target boundary below; none discovers, invokes or authorizes the other targets. The caller preserves nesting under D461/D467 and advances only after a verified applied or no-op result with required recording. It stops on the first failed, refused or uncertain result, retains earlier completed effects and leaves remaining targets untouched, without automatic retry or cross-Atom rollback. One completed Run proves only its bound target; the caller reports the whole cascade complete only after every selected target has a verified result.

### Nodes and entry

The graph has exactly two Step nodes: CA-O-145 and CA-O-129. An admitted Update request enters CA-O-145; admitted Create, Replace or Change Status requests enter CA-O-129. Unsupported request kinds end blocked without an effect.

### Typed transitions and terminal results

| Source Step result | Workflow-owned scheme |
| --- | --- |
| O145: identity-preserving | ON_RESULT O145→O129, subject to current authorization, compatible exact assessment and effect admission. |
| O145: replacement-required | End this Run with an R1520 terminal handoff to the Replace entry of CA-O-127 in a separately admitted Run. Do not call/wait for replacement, perform an intermediate update or treat the handoff as replacement permission. |
| O145: unresolved, invalid, stale, unauthorized or unavailable | End blocked with the exact evidence/decision gap; no approval inferred. |
| O129: reassessment-required for Update | ON_RESULT O129→O145 only with an explicitly admitted fresh proposal/evidence binding and remaining applicable retry allowance. Without them end blocked. |
| O129: applied or no-op | End complete only for the exact admitted boundary with verified results and all required durable Run/change receipts; no-op reports no Artifact change. |
| O129: invalid, stale, unauthorized, unsupported, blocked, recording-blocked, failed, partial or canceled | End with that truthful non-complete outcome, actual completed/incomplete effects and recoverable evidence; no automatic replay. |

The two ON_RESULT edges have Step endpoints in this Workflow. No other route, implicit retry, continuation, graph node or Action-selected successor is admitted. A changed definition pauses dispatch for R1525 revalidation; completed effects and retry accounting remain retained.

## Details

Reuse O067 identity assessment through O145 and O051 accepted replacement persistence through the effect Action. The graph neither duplicates those behaviors nor owns their bindings. A Summary change always follows the replacement-required terminal route; a changed proposal or stale evidence requires reassessment before update persistence.

The separately admitted successor obtains fresh definition/input/permission bindings. Required pending replacement is not reported complete. Change Status resolves the actual current Atom, then its complete Content Role and optional Type-qualified model: use the applicable existing whitelist and transition rule under R1521/R1308, including current Operations R1874 and Analysis R1875 role bindings, not a Workflow list. A more-specific declared Role/Type model overrides its role model; otherwise the role model applies without duplicated Type value sets. A same current status is a no-op. Archive is only a shortcut when that qualified model explicitly defines an archival status; otherwise archive ends missing-archival-model/unsupported without mapping Concern resolved or canceled to archival meaning.

Every Workflow/Step/Action Run, including referenced Action executions, standalone use, nested lineage, failure/cancellation and no-op, retains exact definitions/inputs, parent references, start/terminal/result/effect evidence in the one authoritative Journal under R1720/R1525 and applicable Run policy. Missing durable receipts are recording-blocked, not journaled success. No secret or competing history store is introduced. This is a source graph, not evidence of implementation, MCP, prompt or runtime execution.

### Behavior and outcomes

1. Reject multiple independent Create/current targets or predecessors as invalid before effects or reuse of an assessment. 2. Create: prove each destination absent and unique and each assigned identity unused against current allocation plus preserved all-history evidence; absent Active files alone are insufficient. 3. Update: consume O067's exact identity-preserving result, not a reimplemented classifier. Preserve identity/Summary and admitted placement; an assessment requiring replacement cannot authorize this effect. Changed proposal, target or evidence returns reassessment-required with no mutation; changed definitions require separate revalidation. R1432 increments Version by exactly +1 for every actual same-ID update, including carrier_only/equivalent refinement and semantic_revision; replacement is not same-ID update. R1788 refreshes Updated At on every actual edit, including formatting; an exact no-op retains Version and Updated At. 4. Replace: validate the complete predecessor→successor-set intent without reducing it to a pair. Do not infer a successor from the predecessor or accept missing, partial, unsealed, colliding, or preexisting successor content. Its exact bound role model (including R1874 for Operations and R1875 for Analysis) supplies values; a more-specific declared Role/Type model overrides it, otherwise it inherits the role model without duplicated Type lists. Its most-specific Delivery rule supplies placement; only after that may D466's conditional Active/current or lowercase-status fallback apply. A missing, ambiguous or unsupported qualified model blocks unchanged; no role borrows another role's values. A same current value returns no-op. A containment cascade required by R1521 is composed by the calling Workflow from separate individually admitted invocations for the parent and each contained Atom's latest Revision; this Action still changes only its one bound Atom. References outside the parent Carrier tree and older archived Revisions are not cascade targets. Retain descendants within that tree when applying their model-admitted placement, including Archived. This source rule does not assert that a selected executor implements cascade composition. Archive only requests a status the same qualified model explicitly defines as archival; absent archival meaning returns missing-archival-model/unsupported unchanged, never maps Concern resolved/canceled or forces Archived. Preserve required identity/Summary/body/history/references, retain exact prior Revision bytes, and serialize only the admitted new current status, Version incremented by exactly +1 and actual edit time while keeping prior transitions in the shared Journal. Applicable archival uses one whole atomic Carrier transition and canonical @version suffix. Invalid models/transitions/destinations are blocked, never approximated by a universal list.
6. Freeze the complete mutation-free proposal and current preconditions. ## Details

Concrete MCP/Tool/path/seal adapters and implementation remain in their existing Engine/configuration units; current R1432/R1788 govern every actual same-ID update and exact no-op, while retained history preserves exact predecessor bytes.

Every actual invocation, including standalone and the referenced O051 execution, retains its distinct Action Run identity, exact definition/input binding, parent Action/Step/Workflow lineage where applicable, start/terminal outcome, results/effects and canonical durable evidence. # Summary

Query and fetch Artifacts

## Action

Query and fetch Artifacts **must** evaluate a caller filter only against one
sealed, allowlisted Markdown-carrier snapshot and return matching canonical
Artifact IDs by default, or only the caller-selected frontmatter properties
and sections when fetch is requested.

## Scope

This Action may be invoked standalone or by CA-O-160 for CA-O-158. An Atom
Artifact carries `atom_id`; every other admitted Markdown Artifact carries
`artifact_id`. Exactly one applicable identity is required; missing,
conflicting, or snapshot-duplicate identity is diagnostic. A filename, path,
or heading never supplies or repairs identity. The Action reads neither credentials
nor secrets and evaluates neither SQL, code, templates, nor arbitrary
expressions.

## Details

1. This Action alone enumerates and retains one ordered, allowlisted snapshot
   within CA-R-1850 budgets before evaluation. Members record safe relative
   path, identity, and digest. Unreadable Markdown, malformed frontmatter,
   identity failure, duplicate frontmatter key/heading path, or incomplete
   enumeration is diagnostic, not an accepted partial result. A continuation
   enumerates nothing: it validates its exact retained member paths, identities,
   and digests or rejects.
2. A frontmatter selector is JSON string `"fm:/<pointer>"`; a section selector
   is `"section:/<level>:<heading>/<level>:<heading>"`. Pointer tokens and each
   complete heading segment use RFC 6901 escaping (`~` -> `~0`, `/` -> `~1`).
   JSON Pointer addresses nested maps and arrays. Namespaces are distinct.
   Explicit null is a value; absent selected field returns `missing`, never null.
3. Apply CA-R-1850's closed JSON grammar. YAML temporal values normalize to
   explicit strings; strings are never dates. Deep typed equality distinguishes
   booleans from numbers, supports arrays/maps, and never coerces values.
4. Apply every caller-selected property and status exactly as expressed; no
   implicit `Active` filter, status narrowing, or property exclusion exists.
   With no fetch selection return only Artifact IDs. With a selection return
   only IDs plus those named values/sections and their explicit `missing` or
   `null` states.
5. Sort matches by canonical Artifact ID in ascending bytewise order. A page
   uses a positive limit no greater than configured `query.max_page_size` and an opaque
   cursor bound to retained snapshot digest and last returned ID. An absent cursor
   starts the first page; a changed, malformed, foreign-snapshot, exhausted, or exact-member-mismatched cursor
   cursor is an error. Every response reports snapshot reference/digest,
   examined count, matched count, returned count, and `has_more`, so coverage
   is truthful and pagination cannot silently cross snapshots.

# Summary

Query the stable Journal Event snapshot

## Operation

This Step is the query node of CA-O-161 and invokes exactly one Action, CA-O-162, Query Journal Events.

### Inputs and parameters

Before workflow/action-start recording or Action dispatch, the adapter captures the selected Project's canonical Journal byte-prefix and binds one opaque snapshot token containing source-root identity, prefix byte length and hash, ordered member references, member byte hashes and actually supplied string Event IDs without deduplication or a unique-ID requirement. Capture every decoded row, including missing/nonstring IDs, repeated IDs, lists and scalars, without changing the recorded JSON. Query result wrappers use None when a string ID is absent; coverage follows actual rows, not Event-ID uniqueness. The Action consumes exactly that sealed frontier. A standalone Action captures before its own Run evidence. Bind the literal filter expression, requested result mode (`ids`, selected `fields`, or `full_events`), selected fields when applicable, and bounded page request. The token excludes this invocation's later Run/Event records and permits later append only outside the sealed prefix.

## Details

The Step accepts no filename identity, secret-bearing selection, arbitrary SQL/code, mutation parameter, or fallback Journal root. A failed or incomplete Action returns its actual diagnostic and does not fabricate a successful Workflow or Action Run.

# Summary

## Operation

Archive Selected Active Atoms **means** the reusable Action that archives one explicit current logical Atom under its applicable lifecycle model, preserving its identity, Summary, content and recoverable history. This Atom lifecycle Action offers no Atom deletion; file cleanup is separately scoped.

### Action

1. bind the exact Atom ID and Version, owning Scope Unit, current Status and private source evidence. Resolve its applicable Content Role/Type archival transition and current permission under CA-R-1521/CA-R-1308. Do not assume a universal Archived value or reinterpret resolved/canceled Concern states as archival meaning.
2. require one eligible current non-archived Atom and an explicitly allowed archival transition. Reject Draft, already archived, missing, ambiguous or stale targets, unavailable archival models and unsafe or occupied destinations before effects.
3. derive its private governed history destination under CA-D-565/CA-D-466/CA-D-289, preserving ID, Summary, body and unrelated metadata. Preserve exact prior Version N bytes as history, and bind the archival effect's allowed lifecycle Status, Version N+1 and actual Project-time updated_at with its corresponding governed basename and historical-resolution checks. Never rewrite the preserved N predecessor.
4. execute only through the current admitted Project-local route with exact sealed permission and rechecked source/destination evidence. Safely perform and verify this one Atom's archival effect, retaining its actual result and required recording.
5. on failure recover only this Action's verified mutable frontier while preserving earlier successful Atoms, pre-existing history and accepted Journal evidence. Retain truthful failed/partial/unknown effects if recovery or recording is incomplete.
6. return the actual archived Atom ID and Version. In replacement 100 -> 200, archival targets and reports 100; it neither reports 200 as the archived target nor automatically changes references from 100 to 200.

For a folder-backed Plan, Workflow or Step, include its matching Directory Carrier in this one Atom's admitted placement map and retain the recursively contained tree under the parent's governed archived placement and matching basename. Preserve exact older Revision bytes and do not migrate noncanonical legacy archive trees. Relocation does not infer or rewrite descendants' Status or Revision metadata. The calling Workflow composes the required R1521 cascade as separate individually admitted Actions for the parent and each selected descendant's latest Revision; this Action neither selects those descendants nor reports their changes complete. Referenced Atoms outside the Carrier tree remain untouched.

### Batch and stop boundary

A requested batch is an ordered list of independently authorized Atom Actions. Invoke one Action at a time; advance to the next distinct explicit Atom only after confirmed success. On the first failure, stop, retain all earlier successful effects and their evidence, and leave the remaining targets untouched. Never roll back earlier successful Atoms to simulate a cross-Atom transaction. Validation, stale-source checks, permissions, safe effects and recovery within the failing Atom Action remain required. Automatic retry or resume of this new batch policy is deferred; existing recording-only recovery must not replay a performed Action.

An archive preview or no-op is not an invented effect. Historical references remain resolvable without an automatic reference rewrite.

## Details

Bind each actual standalone **or** nested Action Run **to** the shared every-Run contract in CA-P-1117 v3, Done CA-P-1443 J01–J08, independently reviewed by CA-P-1451: exact admitted definition Revision, actual Run identity/lineage, safe input/result/effect references, start, truthful terminal **or** still-pending interruption, **and** durable canonical Journal receipts under CA-R-1720. # Summary

Update sealed CAPRMEDIO Atom carriers

## Operation

Update Sealed Atom Carriers **means** the reusable Action that performs one explicit admitted same-identity edit to one logical Atom under CA-R-866. Each Action preserves ID, Summary, Type and unrelated values; its private Carrier and history effects remain safely validated. A batch does not become one cross-Atom transaction.

## Details

This workflow-facing Action addresses logical Atoms by Atom ID and Version and Scope Units by their declared identity. Carrier paths, filenames and serialization are private implementation details, not public selectors. Resolve current authoritative sources and retain exact private source evidence without inferring a missing or ambiguous identity. No implicit search, successor allocation or reference retargeting is part of an explicitly targeted Action.

### Explicit Property and Section edits

- use exactly one edit family for the Action. A Property edit under CA-R-1934/CA-M-374 adds, replaces or removes one named Property; a list edit adds or removes individual explicit values, replaces one uniquely identified current value, or replaces the complete set. Caller-supplied list indexes are rejected. Missing or ambiguous current values, duplicate results and unsupported cardinality or value types stop before effects.
- a Section edit under CA-R-1933/CA-M-373 addresses exactly one explicit Section and adds, replaces, removes, renames its title or reorders it. The explicit position for reordering is a Section position, not a Property-list index. Preserve every unrelated Section and Property and all required content/structure rules.
- validate the whole proposed Atom under its current Content Role/Type and owning authority before writing. Do not accept mixed families, hidden search or unrelated changes. Any Summary-value change, including wording-only, or Type change returns replacement-required and leaves the target unchanged; this same-ID Action neither allocates a new ID nor archives the predecessor implicitly.
- reference modification is an explicit Property use with exact target ID/Version, current reference value and requested new value. No implicit Find, retargeting to a replacement successor or mutation of other referencing Atoms is admitted.

### Workflow-owned policy and connector boundary

Identity, Summary/Type replacement classification, Version/time, Status, history, semantic validation, authorization and independent-target progression are owned by this workflow feature, not inferred by a mechanical connector. Any selected connector delegation uses D625's explicit logical `modify` request with supplied target, complete delta/content, expected_state and authorization/context; D527's outer transport is unchanged. This definition does not add a runnable binding.

### Per-Atom effect and batch boundary

On the first failure, stop, retain all earlier successful effects and their evidence, and leave the remaining targets untouched. Never roll back earlier successful Atoms to simulate a cross-Atom transaction. Validation, stale-source checks, permissions, safe effects and recovery within the failing Atom Action remain required. Automatic retry or resume of this new batch policy is deferred; Journal append/read never replays a performed Action and introduces no automatic recording retry or recovery.

Resolve the current original and exact proposal, recheck admitted identity classification and actual authority, and retain the mutation-free preview before execution. Apply only through the existing admitted Project-local route with its exact sealed permission, selected Session, completed required assessment and actual Action start retained in the selected Run. A direct call, caller Boolean, candidate acceptance or local preview grants no effect permission. Bind and recheck the source, proposal, validation, definition, destination and history evidence before the one-Atom effect.

Every actual same-ID Atom change, including Status-only, carrier-only and equivalent refinement, advances exactly from Version N to N+1 and records actual Project-time updated_at. Preserve the exact prior N bytes as history without rewriting their metadata. A no-op retains Version/time and creates no history or change event. Identity classification remains required, but it cannot exempt an actual change from this Version rule. Preserve Summary, identity, intended Status, unrelated bytes and prior semantic history. Recover only the verified mutable frontier and attempt-owned history of this Action on its failure; preserve pre-existing history, earlier successful Atoms and accepted Journal evidence. ### Subject-only preview and staged candidates

The closed Subject preview root remains `{atoms, subject_profile?}`; each selected logical Atom has pinned identity/Version/source evidence and explicit `subject_patches`. A patch names governs or depends_on, exact old/current value and explicit new value. Resolve a dependency replacement by its unique current value and reject a caller index, missing/ambiguous old value, resulting duplicate or mixed body/complete-frontmatter request. Syntax checking neither establishes meaning nor chooses a mapping.

Omission selects legacy; approved is explicit. Reuse the selected profile's current grammar evidence for both source and result. Preserve Atom/atom case distinction, reject unsupported forms, and retain private exact scalar-span evidence. Validate complete source and result, preserving every unrelated byte and intended Status. Independently read back bytes/hashes, validate at the original logical source context, and repeat the same pinned preview/time check before returning its closed manifest. Source drift refuses success; partial failures retain truthful artifact references without unsafe cleanup.

Staging performs no authoritative, archive/history, Journal, promotion or MCP effect. It does not create source effect-time evidence, bypass the standalone apply guard, change the staged-only migration scope or reopen deferred live changed-Subject publication. New contract authoring is not implementation or runtime readiness; affected use still needs the independently verified realization.

### Admitted one-target Subject effect

The existing selected update route retains its completed current Analysis Report and exact O067/O145 assessment, O129 lineage, actual selected Session and actual O030 Action start retained in the selected Run. Reopen those persisted bindings; a matching assessment hash alone is insufficient. For the one admitted target, bind deterministic intended Subject bytes with old Version/time, execution-time metadata rule and exact predecessor destination; no-op preserves them. Effect-time materialization and actual current/history readback remain distinct from illustrative preview and intent.

1. Before the publication window, stage and review the exact admitted source-bound change, retaining the existing sealed source/delta/intent, completed assessment, permission and Run evidence. Reopen the review evidence; a candidate or manifest is not an approval token. Candidate time remains illustrative and the existing actual-effect metadata materialization rule is unchanged.

This model does not exclude other Engine writers. Existing safety requirements remain unchanged. The model adds no public request fields, Boolean approval, local writer, transport or new retry/recovery framework.

### Selected Subject publication failure envelope

Successful source-effect completion requires all admitted current/history postconditions; Journal append/read is not permission, proof or a completion gate. For caught publication/postcondition errors, retain the exclusive window while attempting exact restoration of the verified mutable before-frontier and removal of attempt-owned history; preserve pre-existing history and accepted Journal evidence. Confirmed restoration reports a failed attempt, not update success. Failed or unverified restoration is partial/unknown. Abrupt crash or interruption is not crash-atomic and remains interrupted: inspect actual affected current/history files and Run evidence before any separately admitted continuation. Never automatically replay an Atom effect. This adds no crash-recovery framework and changes no other Action's safety boundary.

Live changed-Subject publication remains blocked under its existing explicit guard until this selected access binding and combined verification are independently accepted. This definition is not implementation or readiness, does not remove that guard, activate MCP, alter native meaning or authorize Core migration.

### Run recording

Retain each actual standalone **or** nested Action Run's exact admitted definition Revision, actual Run identity/lineage, safe input/result/effect references, start **and** truthful terminal **or** still-pending interruption under the existing shared Run contract. Workflow-contained bindings also follow CA-R-1525; standalone coverage remains the selected Epic obligation. Preserve existing entries **and** truthful I/O failures; never fabricate a baseline **or** replay an effect. ### Direct Subject preparation Tool calls

CA-D-425's atom_update MCP provider admits only preview_subjects and stage_subjects, separately from selected update_atom. They reuse this definition's preparation policy but are not actual Atom-update Action Runs. These direct calls preserve the existing no-Journal local preparation policy: no Session/Run/event receipt, source Version/time change, archive, promotion or publication is claimed. Actual enclosing-Step Tool-call recording remains required. Local no-MCP statements above describe the CLI, not this separately declared direct binding. Existing update_atom assessment, actual Action-Run observation, trusted-host confirmation, exclusive window, restoration and live-publication guard remain unchanged. Scratch failure retains truthful artifact evidence; a preview hash or candidate never grants effect permission.

# Summary

Deliver current Implementation Workflow prompt carriers

## Scope

the future reviewed prompt package at `102_FRAMEWORK_ENGINE/202_AGENTIC/202_PROMPTS/ACTION_PROMPTS/IMPLEMENTATION_WORKFLOW/`.

## Claim

the package **must** contain only `CA-O-091`, `CA-O-092`, `CA-O-093`, `CA-O-094`, `CA-O-095`, `CA-O-096`, and `CA-O-099` `.prompt.md` carriers, plus `README.md`, `source_bindings.json`, and `tests/`.

## Details

Each prompt header carries exact Step, Action, and context. This Delivery specifies future reviewed carriers and does not authorize changes to current prompt files.

Every invocation packet additionally carries exactly one `selected_project`
binding before a prompt can verify its governed sources or call an Agent:

| Field | Required value | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `selected_project.kind` | `selected_project` | identifies the Project frozen by the selected Workflow; it is not an absolute host path, current directory, code-root copy, or mount grant |
| `selected_project.source_root` | `.caprmedio_caprmedio` | the only authority root for prompt-source resolution |
| `selected_project.source_references` | the exact current `source_bindings` rows, each with Atom ID, Version, project-relative `path`, and SHA-256 | every path is nonempty, relative, has no `..` segment, begins under `source_root`, and resolves only beneath the frozen selected Project |
| `method_projection` | the existing full active-M Projection with source identity, revision, path, digest, and content | its Method source rows must be current members of the same selected-Project source binding; it remains derived input, not Method authority |
| `workspace` | the existing absolute, non-symlink disposable workspace supplied to the Agent | no source binding infers or substitutes this path |
| `permissions.implementation_workspace` | the existing exact `{kind: disposable_workspace, path: workspace, allow_write: true}` capability | it must match `workspace`; this Delivery adds no write grant |

The selected Workflow runtime resolves `selected_project` only from its frozen
Project context. Absent, stale, duplicate, mismatched, escaping, or
partially-readable source references, an incomplete Method Projection, or a
missing/mismatched workspace capability blocks before Agent launch or effects.
This binding exposes neither credentials nor an Agent endpoint and does not
authorize a hidden mount, arbitrary writer, or live-model execution. An
explicit executable mock remains `mock-not-live-llm` evidence only.

# Summary

Serialize Project Settings Content in TOML

## Scope

the Project Settings TOML Carrier.

## Claim

the Project Settings TOML Carrier **must** encode Operator-editable Project initialization inputs through sections **and** fields specified by Standard-tier Atoms under its Core content **and** authority boundaries **and** applicable General settings specifications; it **must not** store Framework Instance choices **or** authoritative Project Structure declarations **or** derived structural values as independently editable settings.

## Details

- the supported current schema **must** use the TOML string `schema_version = "2.0"`. its complete root **must** contain **only** the required `schema_version`, `project`, `artifacts`, **and** `paths` keys **and** optional `project_mcp`.
- `project` **must** be a table containing required `name` **and** optional `obsolete_names`, **and no** other keys. `project.name` **must** be a nonempty TOML string containing the exact lowercase Operator-selected Project Name under CA-D-375.
- **if** present, `project.obsolete_names` **must** be a TOML array of nonempty strings containing the exact registered prior names. an empty array is permitted; absence **and** an empty array **must** remain distinct. preserve their exact values **and** order; do **not** trim, normalize, deduplicate, exclude the canonical name, **or** invent missing prior names. CA-D-392 continues to govern their Projection exposure, **not** this input signature.
- `artifacts` **must** be a table containing **only** the required `identity` table; `artifacts.identity` **must** contain **only** required `project_prefix`. `artifacts.identity.project_prefix` **must** be a nonempty TOML string containing the exact uppercase Operator-selected Atom prefix under CA-D-376 **and** CA-D-378.
- `paths` **must** be a table containing **only** required `control_root`. `paths.control_root` **must** be the TOML string `.caprmedio_<project.name>`, identifying that selected Project's direct-child control root under CA-D-364 **and** CA-D-520; it **must not** override the selected Project **or** declare independently editable Structure.
- **if** present, `project_mcp` **must** be a table containing **only** required `http_port` **and** optional `tool_blacklist`. the selected Project's fixed MCP HTTP port remains governed by CA-D-594. `project_mcp.http_port` **must** be an exact TOML integer, **not** a boolean, **in** `1..65535`. absence of `project_mcp` is permitted for ordinary Settings Read; MCP launch **or** reuse still requires its configured port under CA-D-594.
- **if** present, `project_mcp.tool_blacklist` **must** be a TOML array of nonempty strings naming exact MCP tools whose exposure is disabled for this Project. preserve exact values **and** order without trimming, normalization, deduplication, wildcard matching **or** implicit names. an empty array is permitted; absence **and** an empty array **must** remain distinct when reading **and** serializing, while both mean no blocked tools. a listed tool **must** be absent from discovery **and** refused on invocation before its handler runs; retain its implementation **and** binding for later reuse. this setting controls MCP exposure only **and** does not remove host invocation **or** grant execution authority. no release-specific default is part of this schema.
- validation **must** cover the complete document **and** reject missing required keys, unknown keys **or** sections at **any** level, wrong TOML value types, duplicate TOML keys, unsupported markers, **or** values violating the requirements above. no legacy compatibility section, open extension field, coercion, default, fallback, automatic case conversion, repair, **or** migration is admitted. rejection **must not** authorize changing **or** deleting the existing Carrier.

# Summary

Encode shared selected Run request and result contract

## Scope

The small caller-facing contract shared by selected capability, MCP, and
adapter implementations. It is a service interface, not a new Workflow.

## Claim

RUN_SUPPORT **must** expose `run_selected_operation(request) -> result` with
the following exact bounded request and result representations.

## Details

- `request.mode` is the closed enum `preview | execute`, defaults to `preview`,
  and only literal `execute` starts work; `apply` and all other aliases are
  invalid. Every request contains the non-empty caller-supplied stable
  `request_id`, one `operation_route`, typed non-secret `parameters`, and
  `parameters_digest`; `target_frontier` (ordered safe refs plus
  `target_frontier_digest`); requested `effects` (typed route-owned effect
  descriptors plus `effects_digest`); and `definition_manifest`
  (`manifest_ref`, `manifest_digest`). The shared contract validates these
  shapes/digests but does not enumerate manifest members or decide route domain
  semantics.
- `source_freshness` is required and contains
  `selected_source_registry_ref`, `selected_source_registry_version`,
  `selected_source_registry_digest`, `selected_binding_ref`,
  and `selected_binding_digest`. It is evaluated against the one canonical
  outer `definition_manifest` reference/digest above; shadow or duplicate
  manifest fields inside `source_freshness` are unknown fields and are rejected
  before any Run or effect. Optional
  `expected_definition_revisions` contains ordered Atom ID, kind, Version,
  safe source path, and digest entries and must match that outer canonical
  manifest. The complete per-route manifest and its source construction remain
  owned by the reviewed selected-source/MCP delivery; this contract consumes
  only its exact reference and digest.
- `initiative` contains sealed identity, human-instruction summary, and safe
  reference. Optional `lineage` contains only actual known lineage. A preview
  returns a sealed read-only `proposal_receipt` and `proposal_receipt_digest`
  that bind `request_id`, route, Initiative reference, source-freshness
  declaration/currentness observation, and every parameters/target-frontier/
  effects/definition-manifest digest. It may report preview currentness or a
  non-start blocker, but never has Run IDs or Event IDs/receipts.
- An `execute` request additionally contains that exact `proposal_receipt` and
  digest, `assigned_action_id`, requested Run identity/identities, and sealed
  `operator_authorization`. Authorization contains its reference/freshness
  evidence and binds the same request ID, route, proposal-receipt digest,
  parameters digest, target-frontier digest, effects digest,
  definition-manifest reference/digest, and source-freshness declaration. The
  service rechecks all declared sources/currentness before dispatch. Unknown
  fields, implicit source selection, ambient authorization, secret inputs,
  missing/stale preview/authorization, or reuse of a `request_id` with changed
  canonical bytes are rejected before effect or Run creation.
- `result` always contains `request_id`, `disposition` (`preview`, `declined`,
  `blocked`, `started`, or `terminal`), the proposal receipt for preview, and
  the `source_freshness` comparison/currentness result. Only a started/terminal
  result contains actual Run IDs and admitted definition bindings; a terminal
  result additionally contains truthful operation outcome/result/effect/report
  refs. Preview and every unstarted disposition have no Run/Event identity.
  Plain Journal append/read records supplied observations independently:
  canonical Event IDs/receipts, prior history and successful logging are not
  dispatch or completion prerequisites. An append failure is reported through
  existing diagnostics without changing the independently observed operation
  outcome. No recording-pending or Journal retry/recovery disposition is
  required; any existing replay disposition describes actual dispatch/effect
  state, never permission to repeat an uncertain effect.
- The service neither decides route-specific domain semantics nor creates a
  second workflow executor. Callers supply their selected route implementation;
  MCP and other adapters reuse this contract and default mutations to preview.

# Summary

Deliver coherent connector interface

## Scope

The concrete logical API representation required by CA-R-1936 and CA-M-376 for every connector under CONNECTOR_TOOLS. API means one coherent caller contract, not a new MCP, HTTP, CLI or other transport.

## Claim

Connectors use the same request/result roles for explicit query, read, create and modify operations. Each connector declares only its supported subset and target kinds; the common vocabulary does not require every connector to implement all four operations.

## Details

### Named direct Subject lookup exception

Only CA-D-424's direct read-only ATOM_SEARCH Subject lookup uses its separately closed public criteria instead of the seven-member inner request. It accepts no caller root, physical selector, authorization/context reference, approval flag or Session ID. The canonical root-bound provider validates the actual definition, grammar, Project boundary and selected-source evidence; no synthetic references or new authorization protocol substitute for those checks. It returns the same four logical result roles with no effects. This direct observation creates no Session, Action Run or Journal record and is not a recorded Action execution; an actual enclosing Workflow retains applicable Tool-call recording. This exception does not change the existing Session-based realization, D527's envelope within the selected service, any other connector operation, or staging/publication admission and recording.

### Logical request

The inner request is one JSON object with exactly `operation`, `target`, `query`, `delta`, `expected_state`, `authorization` and `context`.

- `operation` is exactly `query`, `read`, `create` or `modify`, and must belong to that connector's admitted subset.
- Exactly one of `target` and `query` is non-null. Query uses `query = {kind, filters}` and null target; the other operations use `target = {kind, identity}` and null query. The admitted operation schema fixes supported logical kinds, identity and filter shapes. Physical filenames, paths, indexes or backend keys cannot substitute for logical identity.
- `delta` is null for query/read. Create supplies the complete explicitly admitted content; Modify supplies the explicitly admitted edits or proposed content. Its operation-specific shape is fixed by the bound schema; it is not an untyped permission to change anything.
- `expected_state` is null for an unpinned Read or carries the exact supplied Version/source-state evidence for pinned or historical Read. Explicit full-ID Atom Read needs no pre-known Version and returns the actual exact Version/state. Target/context fixes the source view; ambiguity fails rather than invoking Find. Modify requires exact expected current state; Create requires expected absence. Query carries its applicable bound source-view evidence, without inventing an Atom Version for a Scope Unit or configuration.
- `authorization` and `context` are references to existing bound permission and execution/source/schema context, not ambient flags, secret payloads or a second authorization protocol. Verify them against the admitted surrounding contract. Preview does not acquire effect permission.

For example, this illustrative unpinned Read contains no authority by itself:

```json
{
  "operation": "read",
  "target": {"kind": "Atom", "identity": "CA-R-863"},
  "query": null,
  "delta": null,
  "expected_state": null,
  "authorization": "bound-permission-reference",
  "context": "bound-context-reference"
}
```

Workflow admission owns schema/domain validation, identity allocation, initial and changed Version/time, Status/lifecycle and replacement decisions. The connector mechanically checks the supplied shape, currentness, permission and validation bindings, then performs only the explicit requested operation. It does not choose defaults, allocate an ID, bump Version, archive/delete an Atom, infer a replacement or rewrite references. The workflow supplies every admitted metadata/content delta. Reject unknown fields, unsupported subsets, unresolved references, stale state and widened scope before the affected operation writes.

Query returns matches, not full content; Read returns the complete identified state. Neither implicitly invokes the other or a mutation. List-entry replacement uses the unique exact current value, not a caller index; whole-set replacement and add/remove use their separately admitted explicit deltas. CA-O-218 supplies complete Configuration Read under CA-D-631; CA-O-204 supplies Modify on the same shared TOML connector. configuration Workflows choose schema **and** source authority.

### Logical result

The inner result is one JSON object with exactly `data`, `current_state`, `effects` and `errors`.

- `data` is the operation's actual matches, complete read state or observed write result; use null when unavailable. Proposed data is explicitly labelled and never reported as an observed effect.
- `current_state` carries the exact observed logical identity, actual Version where applicable and source-state evidence; use null where state is unavailable. An unpinned Atom Read returns its actual exact Version/state token.
- `effects` is an array of attributable descriptors `{operation, target, state, evidence}`. `state` is `known` or `unknown`; evidence binds actual observations or the unresolved boundary, never a proposed effect. Query, Read and truthful no-op have no mutation effects.
- `errors` is an array of `{code, message, field}`; `field` is the affected logical request field or null. Stable codes are `input_invalid`, `unsupported_operation`, `target_not_found`, `target_ambiguous`, `stale_state`, `permission_denied`, `schema_invalid`, `backend_failure` and `effect_uncertain`. Empty matches are not errors. A failure never erases an earlier observed effect or converts an unknown effect into success. Every unknown effect requires an `effect_uncertain` error. Nonempty errors never indicate success, even when known effects occurred; empty errors require a verified declared result, not merely absence of an exception. A true no-op must verify the requested state unchanged.

Within the existing selected service, place the logical request in CA-D-527's typed parameters and the logical result in its route-owned outcome/result payload. Reuse its parameters/target/effect/definition/currentness/authorization bindings and outer disposition/recording rules unchanged. This carrier introduces no second outer request/result, Run/Event schema, execution engine or admitted route.

### Delivery status

This is an unimplemented required contract awaiting functional verification. Existing individual executable paths remain explicit adapter bindings; the new FEATURE Delivery root is future/unmaterialized and does not relocate code. A replaceable backend contract is not a DB implementation or a guarantee stronger than observed file/TOML behavior. No new retry/resume, concurrency or publication design is admitted. Old fixtures, source pins, installed copies and receipts are historical evidence, not proof of this revision.

# Summary

Deliver declared Scope Unit query data

## Scope

The operation-specific inner request/result representation for Scope Unit Query, refining CA-D-625-CONNECTOR_TOOLS-CORE-DELIVERY--deliver-coherent-connector-interface.

## Claim

Scope Unit Query data **must** use the common closed interface with the concrete logical refinements below. this representation admits no physical backend selector **or** second outer transport.

## Details

### Request refinement

Keep exactly the seven common outer-inner keys; `operation = "query"`, `target = null`, `delta = null`, and `query = {kind: "Scope Unit", filters}`.

`filters` has exactly `frontier`, `predicates` and `result_fields`:

- `frontier = {identity, include_self, include_descendants}`. Identity is the canonical Scope Unit Name in the Project fixed by `context`; both inclusion fields are explicit booleans and at least one is true. The canonical Project Name selects the implicit root; root plus explicit descendants permits a whole-Project frontier. No omitted frontier or physical path is admitted.
- `predicates` is an array of exactly `{field, match, value}` objects, combined conjunctively. Fields are `scope_unit_name`, `scope_unit_type`, `scope_unit_label` or `parent`. Name and Label admit case-sensitive literal `exact`, `prefix`, `suffix` and `contains`; Type and parent admit only `exact`. Values are nonempty strings; Type is `Ordered` or `Unordered`. Parent is a canonical Name in the bound Project, not a path or the private serialized root sentinel. Empty predicates apply only the explicit frontier.
- `result_fields` is an explicit duplicate-free array drawn from those four fields plus `structural_level`, `local_order` and `navigational_order_number`. Identity is always returned. Facts absent under the applicable declaration schema remain absent; missing Type/Label on the root is not invented and does not satisfy a predicate on that field.

Context binds the exact owning Project, source view, applicable schema and source authority. `authorization` binds existing read permission. `expected_state` may be null for an unpinned current view; when supplied, it is the exact existing source-state evidence binding for the selected view, including historical evidence where requested. It is not an Atom Version or a new token protocol. Current versus historical selection is explicit in context, never inferred from filenames.

### Result refinement

Keep exactly `data`, `current_state`, `effects` and `errors`. Available `data = {matches, coverage}`; matches are canonical-name-ordered `{identity, facts}` objects containing only requested facts. `coverage = {frontier, complete}` records the admitted logical frontier and whether all required sources and predicates were checked. A valid empty query has `matches = []`, complete coverage and no errors. Incomplete coverage cannot have empty errors.

`current_state` carries the observed bound Project/source view and exact existing source-state evidence, with no invented Scope Unit Version. Root identity comes from Project Settings; non-Project facts follow CA-D-442-CORE_META_MODEL--encode-scope-unit-declaration-fields. Logical parent facts resolve the declared root sentinel to the actual canonical Project Name. Carried source data and missing optional fields are not repaired.

The error vocabulary and `{code, message, field}` shape are exactly those of CA-D-625-CONNECTOR_TOOLS-CORE-DELIVERY--deliver-coherent-connector-interface: malformed input uses `input_invalid`; unresolved frontier uses `target_not_found`; duplicate or conflicting identity uses `target_ambiguous`; invalid declaration schema/graph uses `schema_invalid`; stale evidence uses `stale_state`; read denial uses `permission_denied`; inaccessible/unavailable backend evidence uses `backend_failure`. Unsupported operation uses `unsupported_operation`. Report available partial matches with incomplete coverage or null data when unavailable, never fabricate complete coverage. Normal Query has `effects = []`; unexpected actual or unknown effects retain the common truthful evidence and fail, with `effect_uncertain` for unknown effects.

CA-D-441-CORE_META_MODEL-GENERAL--encode-the-project-structure-document-schema and CA-R-1484-CORE_META_MODEL-GENERAL-REQUIREMENT--establish-scope-units-through-project-structure-declarations retain declaration authority. This is an unimplemented source representation pending independent acceptance; CA-O-211-CONNECTOR_TOOLS-STANDARD-ACTION--query-declared-scope-units is its operation definition, not a new CLI/MCP/HTTP route. The existing selected service uses the unchanged common outer envelope where applicable.

Read Engine settings through one shared boundary

## Scope

apply **when** PROGRAMMATIC behavior depends on Project Settings.

use one centralized Settings Reader for **every** applicable Tool, App, **and** MCP
component. the Reader reads the authoritative Project Settings Artifact,
validates the complete input, **and** returns an immutable typed snapshot with
the actual validated values, exact selected Project, physical source path,
raw SHA-256 Digest, **and** declared schema marker. the Reader **must not** query

is derived; Project Settings is **not** a Projection.

   **or** application service.

   fallbacks, semantic overrides, **or** writes **to** the Reader.
5. make the control panel use the same Reader **and** request changes **to** the
   authoritative Project Settings Artifact through its dedicated Doer, **not**
   through the Reader, its immutable snapshot, **or** a Projection.

### Outcome

**every** component observes one validated settings snapshot **without** duplicating
parsing **or** inventing a second control panel.

### Failure or stop

stop **when** the authoritative Project Settings Carrier is missing **or** schema-invalid,
mandatory physical source path **or** Digest provenance is absent, **or** a consumer

Find, Read and Modify **must** be independent logical operations. Find returns matching Atom or Scope Unit identities and matching facts; Read obtains the complete explicitly selected source with its exact identity and Version or revision; Modify accepts explicit targets and does not silently Find or replace them. CreateAtom and CreateScopeUnit are explicit logical creation operations. Workflows **must** express these operations in Atom and Scope Unit terms; storage connectors own the private mapping to Markdown, TOML, files, database records or another backend. Workflows bind the coherent logical connector interface, not paths, tables or backend query languages. Existing path, filename, frontmatter, content, exact-selector, output-view, and lifecycle behavior remains available. Subject lookup reads only valid current Atom files with a canonical flat `subjects` block; invalid source paths, symlink targets, projections, malformed carriers, duplicate fields/values, and owner/path disagreements are rejected or diagnosed without widening selection. Prefix matching ends only at a declared Subject delimiter, so a value such as `Artifact/Atom` does not match `Artifact/Atomology`.

The output carries one source pin per occurrence and no inferred target or native graph edge. The local CLI remains mutation-free: it performs no write, rename, repair, migration, Projection rebuild or history/Journal effect. The direct MCP delivery below is a required realization, not a claim of completed registration or live acceptance. CA-R-863 and CA-O-046 remain the governing Requirement and Action; CA-M-370 supplies the focused authoring method when that Method carrier is delivered.

### Direct read-only Subject MCP delivery

The canonical provider must declare this existing Tool binding and expose strict closed request/result models through the descriptor-driven MCP registry. Root is bound by the registry, never supplied by a caller. Descriptor hints do not replace canonical source validation.

```toml

mcp_name = "atom_search"
```

The public `SubjectLookupRequest` requires exactly `subject`, `subject_field`, `subject_match`, `subject_profile`, `scope_unit`, `content_roles` and `lifecycle`, with optional `atom_ids`. Required fields have no defaults. All models reject unknown fields and coercion. `subject` is nonempty text; fields are governs/depends_on/both, modes exact/prefix/suffix/contains and profiles legacy/approved. Exact/prefix criteria are valid complete expressions under the selected profile; suffix/contains criteria may be nonempty literal fragments. Complete selected source Subjects remain profile-validated.

`scope_unit` is one registered owning Scope Unit name, not a new stable-ID or physical-path scheme. `content_roles` is an explicit nonempty unique array from Concern/Analysis/Plan/Requirement/Method/Evaluation/Delivery/Operations. `lifecycle` explicitly selects active/draft/archived/done/resolved/canceled/all using the existing private lookup inclusion rules; all intentionally includes the wider lifecycle set rather than silently choosing current-only. Optional `atom_ids` contains unique complete logical Atom IDs; omission or an empty array imposes no extra ID restriction. No caller root, under, path, filename, index, body query, context/authorization reference, approval flag, Session ID or preview/execute option is accepted. Unsupported Type, target Scope Unit, arbitrary projection and other generic Find filters fail rather than widen the request.

The public `SubjectLookupResult` has exactly `data`, `current_state`, `effects` and `errors`. On complete success, data is exactly `{matches, complete: true, subject_profile, subject_profile_evidence}`. Each match is exactly `{atom_id, version, status, current_scope_unit, updated_at, field, value}`; field is governs or depends_on, and separate matching fields remain separate rows. Sort by Atom ID, Version, field and exact value. No full Atom content, private path or dependency index is returned.

Current state is an array of unique `{identity, version, source_token, source_view}` records per matched carrier, preserving historical Versions; source_token is the complete-byte SHA-256 and source_view is exactly `{scope_unit, content_roles, lifecycle}`. Profile evidence is exactly `{grammar_pins, native_admission: not_performed}`, with each public pin exactly `{atom_id, version, sha256}`; physical pin paths remain private. Effects are always an empty array. Errors follow D625's exact code/message/field schema. A complete empty match returns empty matches/state/errors. A selected-source diagnostic, ambiguity, stale or incomplete frontier, unsupported input or exceeded read budget returns null data/current_state and nonempty errors; partial results are not successful complete coverage.

Validate current Delivery/Action and applicable Requirement/Method/shared definition pins, the selected grammar pins, Project settings/structure and selected-source evidence. Use bounded no-follow reads, preserve possible selected-current-ID collision checks without full admission of unrelated excluded C/A, and recheck source bytes and inventory before returning. Static reported hashes alone are insufficient. Do not require absent Type on otherwise eligible selected R/M/D sources.

Only this direct read-only Subject realization uses D625's named request-envelope exception. It creates no Session, Action Run, Journal or scratch staging artifact and grants no mutation permission. A real enclosing Workflow remains responsible for applicable Tool-call recording. Existing CLI and Session-based behavior, and all preview/staging/publication admission, remain unchanged. Installed binding/code refresh and actual registered/connected-MCP acceptance are separate from this source declaration.
